deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Graph and quantum foundations

Reading order: these are the introductory derivations originally written before the quantum implementation. The implemented versions, actual settings, limitations and checks are detailed in the Phase D–F sections below. The historical three-question baseline did not execute QAOA.

Graph features and complementarity

An entity/relation graph might contain Film A → directed by → Maya Rao and Maya Rao → born in → Jaipur. Its edges need source provenance. An entity-link graph based only on shared mentions is a simpler structure and must not be described as verified semantic relations.

The optimizer instead uses a graph whose nodes are passages and whose edges are pair interactions. Features from the first graph may determine coefficients in the second:

Egraph(x)=−α∑irixi+∑i<j(βSij−ηCij)xixj.E_{\mathrm{graph}}(x) =-\alpha\sum_i r_i x_i +\sum_{i<j}(\beta S_{ij}-\eta C_{ij})x_i x_j.Egraph​(x)=−αi∑​ri​xi​+i<j∑​(βSij​−ηCij​)xi​xj​.

Cᵢⱼ estimates complementarity; η controls its weight. Shared entities alone are insufficient to establish it. Aliases, extraction mistakes and irrelevant paths can create misleading connections. Coefficients must come from allowed question/text inputs and development-frozen rules.

Graph features are a scoring change. Evaluating them classically first isolates whether they improve the model of useful evidence before circuit behavior complicates interpretation.

QUBO and Ising mapping

For a binary energy with strict upper-triangular pair coefficients:

E(x)=∑iaixi+∑i<jbijxixj,xi=I−Zi2.E(x)=\sum_i a_i x_i+\sum_{i<j}b_{ij}x_i x_j, \qquad x_i=\frac{I-Z_i}{2}.E(x)=i∑​ai​xi​+i<j∑​bij​xi​xj​,xi​=2I−Zi​​.

Z has eigenvalue +1 on bit 0 and −1 on bit 1. First substitute into a linear term and then a pair term:

aixi=ai2I−ai2Zi,bijxixj=bij4(I−Zi−Zj+ZiZj).a_i x_i=\frac{a_i}{2}I-\frac{a_i}{2}Z_i, \qquad b_{ij}x_ix_j=\frac{b_{ij}}4 \left(I-Z_i-Z_j+Z_iZ_j\right).ai​xi​=2ai​​I−2ai​​Zi​,bij​xi​xj​=4bij​​(I−Zi​−Zj​+Zi​Zj​).

Collect the constant pieces, every coefficient touching one qubit, and every two-qubit coefficient. This yields:

HC=cI+∑ihiZi+∑i<jJijZiZj,H_C=cI+\sum_i h_i Z_i+\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}Z_i Z_j,HC​=cI+i∑​hi​Zi​+i<j∑​Jij​Zi​Zj​,
c=12∑iai+14∑i<jbij,Jij=14bij,c=\frac12\sum_i a_i+\frac14\sum_{i<j}b_{ij}, \qquad J_{ij}=\frac14 b_{ij},c=21​i∑​ai​+41​i<j∑​bij​,Jij​=41​bij​,
hi=−12ai−14(∑j<ibji+∑j>ibij).h_i=-\frac12a_i -\frac14\left(\sum_{j<i}b_{ji}+\sum_{j>i}b_{ij}\right).hi​=−21​ai​−41​(j<i∑​bji​+j>i∑​bij​).

The constant does not change which bitstring minimizes energy, but it matters when comparing reported Hamiltonian energies with the original objective. During state evolution it produces only a common global phase, which the circuit can omit while energy evaluation retains the offset. The binary and Ising expressions give the same computational-basis energies.

For a = (−1,−0.5) and b₁₂ = 0.2, c = −0.7, h = (0.45,0.2) and J₁₂ = 0.05. Substitution gives energies 0, −1, −0.5 and −1.3 for bits (0,0), (1,0), (0,1) and (1,1). These values were checked algebraically and numerically. They are illustrative mapping checks, not quantum execution results.

Qiskit labels qubit 0 as the least significant bit. Integer state 1 therefore means x_0=1 and all other x_i=0. The energy table forms bit i as (state_index >> i) & 1. A displayed bit string must be interpreted with this convention; reversing it incorrectly would choose different passages.

Before mapping a constrained selection problem, handle its constraints. One option adds λ(sum xᵢ − k)²:

λ(∑ixi−k)2=λ[(1−2k)∑ixi+2∑i<jxixj+k2].\lambda\left(\sum_i x_i-k\right)^2 =\lambda\left[(1-2k)\sum_i x_i +2\sum_{i<j}x_i x_j+k^2\right].λ(i∑​xi​−k)2=λ[(1−2k)i∑​xi​+2i<j∑​xi​xj​+k2].

Every pair receives a penalty coupling. Removing semantic edges therefore need not make the complete circuit sparse. A cardinality-preserving mixer avoids this particular penalty formulation but introduces its own preparation and mixing costs.

QAOA and classical parameter optimization

The standard variational structure alternates a cost Hamiltonian H_C and mixer H_M, following the original QAOA formulation:

∣ψp⟩=Up⋯U1∣ψ0⟩,Uℓ=e−iθℓHMe−iφℓHC.|\psi_p\rangle=U_p\cdots U_1|\psi_0\rangle,\quad U_\ell=e^{-i\theta_\ell H_M}e^{-i\varphi_\ell H_C}.∣ψp​⟩=Up​⋯U1​∣ψ0​⟩,Uℓ​=e−iθℓ​HM​e−iφℓ​HC​.

The classical optimizer adjusts the angles to reduce the expected energy:

L(φ,θ)=⟨ψp∣HC∣ψp⟩.\mathcal L(\varphi,\theta)=\langle\psi_p|H_C|\psi_p\rangle.L(φ,θ)=⟨ψp​∣HC​∣ψp​⟩.

For a fixed circuit, M measurement samples give an estimator:

L^=1M∑s=1ME(x(s)).\widehat{\mathcal L}=\frac1M\sum_{s=1}^{M}E(x^{(s)}).L=M1​s=1∑M​E(x(s)).

Sampling uncertainty, optimizer behavior and physical noise are separate issues. Minimizing expectation is also different from guaranteeing that a finite sample contains the best feasible bitstring.

The retired prototype wrapper used StatevectorSampler, COBYLA and default p = 1 with a maximum-iteration setting of 50. It is preserved in the release history. The current quantum implementation builds actual circuits and evaluates their statevector/shot objectives directly, with its own recorded budgets. Both approaches simulate quantum states classically; neither is quantum hardware. COBYLA adjusts circuit angles, not LLM parameters. The IBM QAOA tutorial provides the algorithmic reference.

COBYLA means Constrained Optimization BY Linear Approximation. It uses function evaluations and local linear models rather than requiring analytical derivatives. Here the function is a circuit-energy estimate and the parameters are angles. Its local search and finite evaluation budget do not certify the global optimum of the circuit-angle landscape. COBYLA documentation

Increasing circuit depth does not guarantee better observed outcomes with a finite optimizer budget and noisy execution. Report shots, parameter evaluations, compilation, constraints and feasibility alongside answer quality.

The legacy exact solver and Qiskit adapters

The retired prototype exact solver wraps NumPyMinimumEigensolver, which computes a lowest eigenvalue/state classically. Its source remains in the release history. The operator for n binary decisions acts on a space of dimension 2ⁿ; implementations can exploit structure, but the method is not a general scalable substitute for MILP. API reference

MinimumEigenOptimizer is the optimization adapter: it maps supported quadratic problems to an operator and interprets eigensolver output as optimization variables. Its name does not identify whether the underlying method uses quantum hardware. Adapter reference

StatevectorSampler simulates state evolution and samples from the resulting distribution. Even with an ideal simulated state, finite samples introduce measurement-sampling variability. This is distinct from physical-device noise. Sampler reference

The new constrained MILP baseline uses none of these eigensolver wrappers. Its optimum is a classical reference for the specified objective, not a demonstrated output from a hypothetical perfect quantum computer.

Sparsification changes the optimization problem

Let the sparse objective retain pair terms through a mask Mᵢⱼ:

E~(x)=∑iaixi+∑i<jMijbijxixj.\widetilde E(x)=\sum_i a_i x_i+\sum_{i<j}M_{ij}b_{ij}x_i x_j.E(x)=i∑​ai​xi​+i<j∑​Mij​bij​xi​xj​.

Both classical and quantum solvers must be evaluated against the original target as well as the surrogate. Otherwise a lower reported energy may merely reflect removal of costs.

Let R be the removed edge set and let δ be the sum of |bᵢⱼ| over R. Every binary product xᵢxⱼ is zero or one. The magnitude of each removed term is therefore at most |bᵢⱼ|, and the triangle inequality bounds their sum:

∣E(x)−E~(x)∣≤δ.|E(x)-\widetilde E(x)|\le\delta.∣E(x)−E(x)∣≤δ.

If both problems have the same feasible set and the sparse solution is ε-suboptimal under the sparse objective, then:

E(x~)≤E~(x~)+δ≤E~(x⋆)+ϵ+δ≤E(x⋆)+ϵ+2δ.E(\widetilde x) \le\widetilde E(\widetilde x)+\delta \le\widetilde E(x^\star)+\epsilon+\delta \le E(x^\star)+\epsilon+2\delta.E(x)≤E(x)+δ≤E(x⋆)+ϵ+δ≤E(x⋆)+ϵ+2δ.

Read the chain one step at a time. First replace the full energy of the sparse solution by its sparse energy plus δ. Second use ε-suboptimality: the chosen sparse solution is no worse than any feasible comparison, including the full optimum, plus ε. Third replace that comparison's sparse energy by its full energy plus δ. Rearranging gives a full-objective gap of at most 2δ+ε.

The feasible set, candidates, budgets, coefficient scale and energy offsets must be the same in both problems. This elementary bound can be loose; it is a sanity check, not a new theorem or an answer-F1 guarantee. A sampled QAOA selection has no known ε certificate unless a separate solver optimum or bound establishes its sparse-objective gap.

Circuit resources must include state preparation, mixers, routing and constraint encoding. Sparsifying interactions generally does not reduce the number of candidate qubits. A statevector simulator stores amplitudes growing as 2ⁿ; raw complex128 storage alone is about 16 × 2ⁿ bytes, before additional simulator memory. Simulation behavior cannot establish practical hardware speedup.

questions: Can a relevance value of 0.8 be interpreted as an 80% chance of containing the answer?
No. It is a cosine similarity between learned representations, not a calibrated support probability.
Why can an exact MILP optimum give a worse answer than relevance ranking?
MILP optimizes a proxy objective. That objective contains no guarantee about the generator or reference-answer correctness.

Inference inputs and reference annotations

The selector receives the question, source text and provenance. The evaluator separately receives expected answers, aliases and annotated support. Giving the selector the answer key would invalidate the comparison. An oracle diagnostic deliberately uses gold support and is explicitly labelled; ordinary inference does not.

Tokens, chunks and embeddings

Tokens are model-specific text units, not words. MiniLM has a limited input length. The main study creates traceable chunks of at most 240 embedding tokens, including special tokens and a bounded title prefix. Long sentences use overlapping windows. All chunk vectors contribute to a normalized document representation; small important facts can still be diluted by averaging.

For unit chunk vectors zjz_jzj​, document vector vvv and unit question vector uuu:

vˉ=1m∑j=1mzj,v=vˉ∥vˉ∥2,ri=u⊤vi.\bar v=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m z_j,\qquad v=\frac{\bar v}{\|\bar v\|_2},\qquad r_i=u^\top v_i.vˉ=m1​j=1∑m​zj​,v=∥vˉ∥2​vˉ​,ri​=u⊤vi​.

With document rows DDD, relevance is r=Dur=Dur=Du and pair similarity is DD⊤DD^\topDD⊤. The vectors have 384 coordinates. Similarity is not the probability of a true answer. A cache avoids repeating an embedding calculation; an index finds stored vectors relevant to a query. These are different tools.

A subset is a binary decision

xi=1x_i=1xi​=1 means passage iii is selected. The full objective is:

E(x)=−α∑irixi+∑i<j(βmax⁡(sij,0)−γCij)xixj.E(x)=-\alpha\sum_i r_i x_i+\sum_{i<j}\left(\beta\max(s_{ij},0)-\gamma C_{ij}\right)x_i x_j.E(x)=−αi∑​ri​xi​+i<j∑​(βmax(sij​,0)−γCij​)xi​xj​.

Relevance is rewarded, positive similarity is a redundancy penalty, and the entity-link proxy CijC_{ij}Cij​ rewards possible complementarity. The final study fixes α=1\alpha=1α=1, β=0.2\beta=0.2β=0.2 and development-selected γ=0.2\gamma=0.2γ=0.2. Only the strict upper triangle is stored, so each pair contributes once.

A fixed-count constraint is ∑ixi=k\sum_i x_i=k∑i​xi​=k. The separate classical token study uses ∑itixi≤B\sum_i t_i x_i\le B∑i​ti​xi​≤B and a nonempty selection. Equal count does not imply equal tokens.

Generation is another model operation

The project uses frozen pretrained MiniLM and Qwen weights; it does not fine-tune them. The same prompt, ordering policy and decoding settings are shared within comparisons. Circuit-angle optimization does not update the LLM.

Evaluation has two different targets

Answer exact match and token F1 evaluate generated text. Document precision, recall and complete support evaluate selected annotations. They cannot be substituted for one another. If multiset token overlap is mmm, predicted token count is PPP and reference count is GGG:

precision=m/P,recall=m/G,F1=2mP+G.\mathrm{precision}=m/P,\quad\mathrm{recall}=m/G,\quad F_1=\frac{2m}{P+G}.precision=m/P,recall=m/G,F1​=P+G2m​.

For “red red blue” versus “red blue blue”, overlap is two and F1 is 2/32/32/3. Dataset-specific normalization, aliases and empty/special-answer rules matter. Mean per-question F1 differs from F1 calculated after pooling tokens. Failed method executions remain zero in answer averages.

chapters.title: Make a fair experiment
chapters.subtitle: Separate a new score from a better solver.
chapters.lead: A convincing result depends on the comparison contract, not just the winning number.
chapters.body:
### The contribution boundary
Passage-set selection, QUBO evidence selection, graph retrieval, QAOA and graph sparsification all have prior work. The project does not invent these foundations or provide a new sparsification theorem. Its candidate contribution is a controlled evaluation of how they interact under context constraints and complete circuit accounting.

The literature matrix is bounded and dated. An exact original-model reproduction of SetR or the closest QUBO selector is not complete; the lexical coverage reference is an explicitly different adaptation. The manuscript needs a refreshed closest-work search and substantive external review before submission.

### Three research questions
1. Does the query-conditioned entity-link feature improve generated answers under the same budget?
2. Does protecting possible evidence links outperform generic sparsification under matched interaction budgets?
3. How do penalty and count-preserving encodings change feasibility, quality and complete compiled cost?

### The comparison contract
Within each condition, share candidate passages, input order, model revisions, prompt policy, decoding and constraints. Evaluate scoring changes with common solvers, and solver changes with common coefficients. Report count and token conditions separately. Candidate reduction must not consult answer annotations.

Freeze development decisions and held-out IDs before inspecting final results. Retain all seeds and failures. Adding a control after a diagnosis is allowed, but it must be labelled exploratory and must not replace the original result silently.

### Uncertainty belongs to questions
Average solver seeds within each question, then bootstrap paired question differences. The final analysis uses 10,000 resamples and 95% percentile intervals. An interval crossing zero does not prove equality. Preserved quality requires an appropriate predeclared noninferiority design; one was not frozen here.

The source documents below include historical venue information. Their dates are snapshots, not a live deadline feed.

deep.label: Full related-work matrix and search limits
deep.html:
Literature comparison and contribution boundary

Checked November 10, 2026. The matrix records primary-source method descriptions; it is not a claim of independent reproduction. Closest work was read beyond the abstract where accessible. Broader rows are abstract-level context and require deeper comparison before submission. Numbers from different generators or pools are not comparable to our experiments.

Primary source Mechanism and experimental object Relationship to this study / reproduction status
QUBO evidence selection, 2026 Requirement support, coverage, redundancy and complementarity; HotpotQA answer evaluation; simulated annealing Closest formulation overlap. Different semantic estimators and budgets prevent an exact reproduction here. No released author implementation was identified on the inspected paper page. A local requirement-coverage adaptation must be labeled an adaptation.
SetR, ACL 2025 LLM identifies information requirements and selects passage sets Establishes set selection as prior work. Author code available; original API/model configuration is not equivalent to a small local model.
GRiever, EMNLP Industry 2025 Low-resource multi-step graph retrieval A graph feature alone is not novel; retrieval must be controlled separately from selection. Not reproduced.
QAOA sparsification, Quantum 2026 Graph sparsification/decomposition for Max-Cut compilation and noise Closest quantum resource overlap. Our signed selection objective and constraints require separate accounting. Not a new sparsification theorem.
RAG, 2020 Learned retrieval plus generation on knowledge-intensive tasks Foundational architecture; our work does not train that original model.
DPR, 2020 Dual-encoder dense passage retrieval Motivates vector retrieval; our frozen MiniLM is a different encoder.
HippoRAG, 2024 Knowledge graph plus personalized PageRank for multi-hop retrieval Demonstrates graph retrieval overlap; not a QAOA selector. Not reproduced.
HippoRAG 2, 2025 Deeper passage integration and online LLM use for memory/retrieval Stronger graph context; outside the laptop baseline scope as an exact reproduction.
GraphRAG, 2024 Entity communities and summaries for global questions Global summarization differs from selecting fixed multi-hop evidence pools.
LightRAG, 2024 Graph and vector structures with dual-level retrieval Relevant engineering/graph comparison; not an interchangeable solver baseline.
RAPTOR, 2024 Recursive clustering/summaries form a retrieval tree Changes retrieval units; cannot attribute its results solely to subset optimization.
Lost in the Middle, 2023 Measures sensitivity to relevant-context position Requires a shared ordering policy and explicit length reporting.
IRCoT, 2023 Interleaves reasoning and retrieval Adds iterative generation/retrieval cost; not part of a frozen-pool solver comparison.
Self-RAG, 2023 Trained reflection tokens control retrieval/generation Requires a different trained model; not reproduced.
Sparse RAG, 2024 Sparse context selection to accelerate RAG inference Compression/selection efficiency is prior work; our claim must concern the quantum encoding tradeoff.
QAOA, 2014 Alternating cost and mixing operators Algorithmic foundation, not our invention; no generic practical advantage follows.
Alternating operator ansatz, 2019 Mixers constrained to feasible subspaces Existing basis for count-preserving mixers. Preparation/mixer costs remain included.
HotpotQA, 2018 Multi-hop questions with supporting sentences Use original sentence IDs and official metric semantics. Supplied pools are not corpus retrieval.
MuSiQue, 2022 Composed questions designed to require connected reasoning Second dataset, answer aliases and paragraph annotations need a separate adapter.

Closest-work reproduction decision

The QUBO paper includes support-estimation and coverage variables beyond the prototype. Copying only its relevance/redundancy terms is not a reproduction of the full method. We will implement a transparent local requirement-coverage comparator and state its estimator differences. SetR's author repository is available, but changing its underlying LLM changes the experiment. Original-model reproduction and independent author-result validation remain limitations unless actually executed.

Candidate contribution

The candidate is a controlled, encoding-aware study: protect question-linked interactions while removing other pair terms; compare matched edge budgets and actual compiled resources; quantify failures when a cardinality penalty makes the circuit dense again. MILP and heuristics identify formulation effects; QAOA identifies behavior under quantum circuit restrictions. Improvements in answer F1, if observed, must be supported by paired records and intervals. Negative results can still reveal where graph protection or encoding fails, but publishability requires a generalizable finding and independent review.

Search limits

Searches covered QAOA/RAG evidence selection, QUBO selection, graph retrieval and sparsification, followed references from the closest paper and inspected newer related retrieval results. This is a 19-source initial matrix, not an exhaustive citation graph or a novelty certificate. The paper must cite any newly identified closer work before submission. No unattributed copied text or author performance numbers are used as local results.

deep.label: Complete frozen experimental protocol
deep.html:
Research protocol

Version 1, frozen before new held-out model evaluation, November 10, 2026.

Questions and scope

H1: Does a query-conditioned entity-link feature improve selection and generated answers under the same budget? H2: At the same retained-edge budget, does evidence-guided sparsification preserve answer quality and full-objective quality better than coefficient-only, degree and random rules? H3: How do compiled resources, feasibility and quality change under a fixed-count penalty versus a count-preserving QAOA mixer?

These are separate questions. A graph improvement is not a solver improvement. QAOA simulation is not hardware speedup. The narrower contribution is an encoding-aware, matched-budget study of evidence-guided sparsification. Novelty remains a bounded literature-search conclusion, not a guarantee that no related work exists.

Data and controls

Use development examples for all parameter decisions. Preserve the earlier inspected HotpotQA material as development/historical evaluation. Prepare new held-out IDs from official development/validation partitions, excluding earlier evaluation IDs and normalized duplicate questions. MuSiQue uses its answerable subset, with train for development and official dev for held-out evaluation. Freeze IDs, order, source revisions and hashes before inference. No hidden-test claim is made.

Primary comparison: same candidates, input order, generator, prompt, decoding, graph features and feasibility constraints. Compare fixed count and token budget in separate experiments. Supply the full candidate text to the generator; use token-safe chunk representations for embedding. Record actual formatted token consumption. Oracle and empty-context results are diagnostics, never normal competitors.

Outcomes and statistics

Primary task outcome: mean per-question answer token F1. Also report normalized exact match, supporting-document recall, complete annotated support, selected count, actual context/input tokens, time, memory, feasibility and failures. Use each dataset's official answer semantics; MuSiQue maximizes over aliases. Do not silently fix reference annotations.

Compare paired differences on the same questions. Bootstrap question IDs (10,000 resamples, seed 20261110), averaging solver repeats within question first. Show 95% percentile intervals and sample sizes. Predeclare principal comparisons, label the remaining comparisons exploratory, and apply Holm adjustment if reporting a family of significance tests. A confidence interval containing zero is not evidence of equality. No noninferiority claim is made without a predeclared tolerance and a suitable bound.

Primary sparsification comparison: evidence-guided versus absolute coefficient retention at half of available nonzero interaction edges, using the same full target objective and frozen graph weight. Secondary edge fractions: 0.25 and 0.75. Include full and gamma=0 controls. Compare MILP and QAOA on the identical quantum subset. Candidate truncation is relevance-based and independent of labels. Larger classical pool results are contextual results, not a direct quantum scaling comparison.

Execution policy

Profile 50 development questions before selecting final run sizes. Target at least 500 held-out examples per dataset for classical generation, with a separately frozen smaller quantum subset. Record every attempted seed and failure. Quantum budget starts at p=1/2, three seeds, 64 parameter evaluations, 1,024 final shots; adjust only on development profiling and freeze actual settings before final runs. No seed is chosen because it wins on held-out data.

Record original and surrogate energies, actual constraint encoding, state preparation, mixer, auxiliary qubits, compiled two-qubit gates/depth, target connectivity and transpiler seed. Include infeasible shots and postselection costs. Ideal, shot-based and noisy simulations are distinct. No quantum hardware is currently allocated.

The laptop is the execution host; no paid services or purchases. Download public datasets/models from their primary hosts. Keep credentials and personal material local. Use checkpoints and avoid exhausting disk or system memory. Resource permission is not a reason to launch an uninformative experiment.

Reporting and changes

Keep unfavorable results. Save failure records and use all attempted questions in primary answer denominators. Specify successful-only resource summaries. Freeze a main evaluation configuration before viewing outcomes; any later scientific change starts a declared new cycle. A method name containing "evidence" is a hypothesis, not proof of preservation.

Maintain a claim-to-artifact map in the final paper package. Submission, authorship approval, independent manual annotation and unavailable hardware remain explicit handoffs. No external messages or submissions are authorized by this protocol.

Development decision recorded before final evaluation

Gamma=0.2 is selected by equal-weight mean development F1 over 100 questions per dataset. Evidence-guided half-edge versus absolute half-edge remains the principal sparsification comparison. Add a same-shot uniform feasible-sampling baseline because n=10,k=5 has only 252 feasible subsets. Report the study as an encoding-aware comparison; no noninferiority tolerance or quantum-superiority claim is adopted. Larger-candidate and corpus results are separately bounded settings.

Secondary complete-gate-cap diagnostic

Before definitive held-out comparison analysis, add a separately labeled diagnostic on the first ten quantum IDs per dataset. Compare absolute and evidence-guided masks under a hard cap of 180 complete compiled line two-qubit gates, using three seeds and the same p=1/64-evaluation/1,024-shot settings. The cap is based on the approximately 177-gate development half-edge results. Search retention fractions from 1 to 0 in steps of 0.05, keep the largest tested feasible fraction, and verify the actual optimized circuit again. Record preprocessing cost and any cap violations/infeasible penalty control. This does not alter the 18-condition primary matrix or create a noninferiority claim.

The secondary formulation control also compares gamma=0 and gamma=0.2 under the same p=1 XY-QAOA settings, first 50 quantum IDs per dataset and three seeds. Its separate configurations are frozen before definitive comparative answer analysis. This tests scoring effects under QAOA as well as MILP; it does not replace the principal half-edge comparison.

Development distribution diagnostic and preparation erratum

A separate numerical study uses the first 20 recorded MuSiQue development coefficient instances, relevance-reduced to 8/10/12/16 candidates with k=5. It trains p=1 XY and penalty circuits with the same 64-evaluation limit and three seeds. Exact statevector probabilities give optimum-hit probability, no-feasible probability and expected best feasible energy at 1/16/64/256/1,024 final draws. This uses no answer labels or additional LLM inference. Average repeats within question; sizes are nested and are not independent replications. Equal final draws do not equal equal total work because uniform feasible sampling has no angle training.

This diagnostic exposed an analytic limitation: with a feasible basis-state start, the first diagonal cost layer is a global phase. At p=1, gamma cannot affect probabilities, although optimizing the mixer angle against different objectives can still change the result. At p=2 only the later cost layer can produce relative phases. A regression check verifies the diagnosis.

Retain the original frozen matrix unchanged. Add the separately frozen preparation control on the same first 50 quantum IDs per dataset. Before cost evolution, apply one fixed pi/4 XY ring sweep to the seeded feasible basis state. This creates a nonuniform feasible superposition and is included in compilation. Compare base/full objectives, p=1/2 full circuits, half-edge absolute/evidence masks, MILP and same-draw random sampling. No preparation parameter is tuned on held-out answers. These post-freeze controls are exploratory and cannot retrospectively become confirmatory principal results. The extension's exact source and composite core/extension identity are archived separately.

deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Reading statistical comparisons correctly

For question q, let d_q be method A's F1 minus method B's F1 after averaging each method's seeds. The estimated difference is the arithmetic mean of d_q across the N common questions. A paired bootstrap samples N question IDs with replacement, recomputes that mean, and repeats 10,000 times. The 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles give the reported 95% interval. Pairing preserves the fact that both methods face the same easy or difficult question.

If three seeds on one question score 1, 0.5 and 0, that question contributes 0.5. It does not become three independently sampled questions. If the last seed fails, its F1 remains zero and the mean is still 0.5. In contrast, missing resource measurements remain missing: inventing a gate count of zero for an unexecuted circuit would also bias a resource mean. Completed circuits with measured zero feasibility do contribute their actual zero.

An interval entirely above zero supports a positive difference under this sample and analysis. An interval spanning zero leaves both positive and negative effects plausible. It does not establish that the methods are equal. Noninferiority would require a chosen acceptable loss and a suitable interval bound declared before looking at the result. This project does not retrospectively invent such a tolerance.

The question is the resampling unit, but source passages and compositional question templates can still be shared across questions. The bootstrap does not model every such cluster. The two generators are from one family, and numerical simulator training is not physical-device execution. These limits restrict generalization even when a difference looks clear. Secondary exploratory tables are not a large collection of independent confirmatory discoveries.

deep.label: Measured claims versus unverified work
deep.html:
Claims and their evidence

This map distinguishes measured findings, mathematical properties and work that remains unverified. It is a review aid, not an independent validation certificate.

Statement Evidence Boundary
53,230 records in 24 complete conditions were audited Final audit, result index Includes 50,290 primary records and separately scoped controls, not 53,230 independent questions
The evidence-guided half-edge benefit is not established HotpotQA, MuSiQue Paired differences -0.0363 and -0.0095; both intervals cross zero. Equality/noninferiority is not established either
Prepared circuits do not establish a consistent guidance gain Prepared HotpotQA, prepared MuSiQue Post-freeze exploratory controls; both guidance intervals cross zero
Lower common objective energy can accompany worse answers Error signatures and examples, JSON Observations, not independent causal annotations; relevance is rescored with the same full coefficients
A first diagonal cost layer on a basis state is global phase Derivation, actual probability regression Mathematical limitation of this ansatz; not a new theorem about all QAOA implementations
Squared cardinality penalties add all-pairs couplings Quantum implementation, resource tables Complete costs are compiler-policy measurements; not proven minimum gate requirements
Uniform feasible sampling is strong at n=10,k=5 Sampling table, numerical evidence 1,024 draws cover one unique optimum with probability about 0.9829; QAOA additionally has angle-training cost
MILP linearization handles both coefficient signs Baseline tests, budget tests Numerical solver certification; larger time-limited cases are not all optimal
Sparse coefficients obey the stated absolute-error bound Derivation, checks No answer-quality guarantee follows from the coefficient bound
Embedding inputs are token-safe and persistent state is checked Retrieval tests, GPU input-length/profile evidence Mean pooling still approximates facts; tested workload is not every possible input
Corpus studies use shared retrieved pools Corpus manifest, restorer Closed union of benchmark inputs; not full Wikipedia or a deployed enterprise corpus
Public statistics and solver cases reconstruct Table reconstruction script, solver smoke evidence Different from rerunning full retrieval and LLM generation
The local API executes real inference and preserves state Service benchmark, recreated-container verification Five repeated fictional comparisons; no production SLA, browser visual approval or prompt-injection guarantee
The PDF was reviewed visually Export QA, PDF All 13 pages inspected for layout; no scientific peer-review claim

Not established: quantum advantage, physical-device performance, a verified factual knowledge graph, general evidence-preservation guarantees, exhaustive novelty, an original-model reproduction of the closest external selectors, independent semantic annotation, publication submission or acceptance. The literature matrix, limitations and handoff make these boundaries explicit.

questions: Why are three solver seeds on 50 questions not 150 independent questions?
The seeds repeat computation on the same questions. They share the question and evidence; average within question before question-level uncertainty estimation.

chapters.lead: Explore the saved comparisons. These charts read tracked analysis artifacts; they do not launch new experiments.
chapters.body:
### Begin with the denominator
The primary matrix contains 18 conditions and 50,290 method/question evaluations over 1,000 distinct held-out questions. Six scoped controls bring the total to 24 runs and 53,230 records: 53,209 successful and 21 failed. Main classical count comparisons use 500 questions per dataset/generator. Main quantum comparisons use 50 per dataset, at most ten candidates and three averaged seeds.

### Four findings to carry forward
**Lexical coverage has the highest observed F1** in all four main classical count settings. That is an observed ranking, not a universal superiority theorem.

**Evidence-guided half-edge sparsification does not establish a benefit.** Evidence-minus-magnitude differences are −0.0363 F1 on HotpotQA and −0.0095 on MuSiQue; both paired intervals cross zero. Prepared controls also fail to establish a consistent benefit.

**Constraint encoding changes resources.** A squared count penalty introduces all-pairs couplings. XY count preservation avoids that particular penalty but adds mixer/preparation costs. Generic synthetic-line compilation is not a minimum-gate proof or a physical timing measurement. The known-basis first cost layer can be redundant; state-aware simplification remains a review concern.

**Lower energy can accompany worse answers.** Full MILP has lower common-objective energy but worse F1 than relevance ranking on 31, 37, 36 and 32 questions across the four main count conditions. This is an observed proxy mismatch, not independent causal annotation of graph or generator errors.

### Comparisons that must stay separate
The 1,200-token conditions use 100 questions, while count conditions use 500. The 25-candidate corpus studies use 100 questions; 50/100-candidate studies use 30. Their raw means do not isolate a causal effect across different populations. Larger one-second MILPs are not all certified optimal. Larger quantum sensitivities are only five MuSiQue questions per size.

### Failures and output limits
One main penalty run produced no feasible sample. Twenty gate-cap diagnostic records could not satisfy the imposed cap; these remain failures. The audit flags 914 successful records reaching the 32-new-token generation allowance, which indicates possible truncation rather than proving every answer is incomplete. These are records, not distinct neural calls.

deep.label: Full definitive evaluation
deep.html:
Phase G — definitive evaluation and independent audit

The 18-condition definitive primary matrix is complete: 50,290 method/question evaluations over 1,000 distinct held-out questions. Separate controls add 800 formulation, 140 gate-cap and 2,000 prepared-circuit records, giving 53,230 records across 24 completed runs. All 24 grids were audited. The primary and formulation runs share the same frozen core source fingerprint; the preparation control adds an explicitly hashed extension. Documentation and service commits changed during execution, so a common scientific source hash is more precise than claiming one repository commit for every run.

The audit recomputed dataset-specific scores, checked IDs/counts/token budgets, summed full and sparse energies independently, verified source/config/data identities and retokenized saved prompts. It independently counted feasible shots from measured bit strings, including failed circuits. The gate diagnostic's retained masks and final complete line circuits were reconstructed and recompiled. Its successful circuits satisfy the 180-gate cap. Audit evidence records every checked condition.

There is one genuine no-feasible-sample failure in the primary matrix: HotpotQA question 5add9bfa5542990dbb2f7e85, penalty-full seed 42. It remains zero in answer averages and zero in completed-circuit feasibility. Twenty additional gate-cap control records reject the penalty encoding because no tested retention level fits the cap; they are explicit diagnostic failures rather than successful substituted executions. No service fallback enters scientific results.

Findings and interpretation

The principal half-edge comparison does not establish an evidence-guidance benefit on either dataset. Both intervals include zero, so neither equality nor noninferiority follows. Lexical coverage has the highest observed F1 in all four 500-question classical count conditions. Graph-minus-base effects vary across settings and their reported exploratory intervals also include zero. These results support a bounded comparative/negative-result account, not a new state-of-the-art or quantum-advantage claim.

Exploratory feasible-superposition control

The frozen XY implementation starts from a basis state. Its first diagonal cost layer contributes only a global phase; at p=1 its cost angle cannot affect probabilities. We retained those results and separately added one fixed pi/4 XY ring sweep before the first cost layer. This creates a feasible, generally nonuniform superposition and makes subsequent cost phases observable after mixing. The added sweep is included in complete compilation. This control was introduced after the analytic diagnosis and is exploratory, not a replacement for the principal frozen comparison.

Objective quality is not answer quality

Across the four 500-question fixed-count conditions, full MILP has lower common-objective energy but worse F1 than relevance selection on respectively 31, 37, 36, 32 questions (HotpotQA 1.5B/3B, MuSiQue 1.5B/3B). The relevance subset is rescored using the full MILP coefficients for this comparison. These observations directly distinguish proxy optimization from downstream correctness; they do not independently identify a causal graph or generator error. Deterministic examples and additional signatures are released.

What can be reproduced without a model

All 24 public prediction tables and their paired intervals reconstruct without loading an LLM or raw dataset. An additional 110-instance coefficient bundle supports solver-only experiments over 100 distinct quantum-subset questions and nested 12/16-candidate sensitivities. It contains no answer/support labels or source text. Four actual solver reproductions match recorded selected indices, full energy and compiled line gates: original full XY, prepared full XY, evidence-sparse XY and a 16-candidate case. Reproduction checks document the scope.

The exact core source snapshot and preparation extension snapshots are released alongside configurations. Full prompts/input IDs remain in the large local run bundles; public restorers rebuild the frozen inputs from primary hosts. Model-free table regeneration is not an independent rerun of answer generation.

The error-signature analysis includes deterministic examples of better common objective values with worse answers. These observations explain why optimizing a proxy does not certify useful evidence. They are not independently annotated causal error labels. Source overlap, imperfect references, weak entity links, a small quantum subset, one generator family and ideal statevector training remain limits.

deep.label: Measured results and boundaries
deep.html:
Generation length limits in the completed evaluation

The final audit records 914 successful method/question outcomes flagged as reaching the 32-new-token allowance across the 24 runs. These are flagged records, not 914 distinct model calls: identical selected contexts within one question can reuse the same generated answer, and questions recur across conditions. Reaching the allowance indicates possible output truncation; it does not prove that every flagged answer is incomplete. These predictions remain scored as emitted under the frozen policy. No longer-answer rerun was substituted after examining scores.

This output-length issue is different from embedding input truncation. The main encoder checks token-safe chunks and rejects overlong queries; generation separately checks the fully formatted prompt against its 4,096-token total allowance. The historical baseline's statement that it had no limit hits applies only to its six outcomes. The final audit also distinguishes 53,209 successful records and 21 failed records; retaining failures in answer averages does not mean every recorded method produced an answer.

deep.label: Distribution and sampling study
deep.html:
Development-derived sampling mechanism study

To separate trained distribution quality from best-of-many selection, we train p=1 circuits on 20 development-derived coefficient instances at each of n=8,10,12,16, with k=5 and three seeds per encoding. These are 480 numerical circuit solves, not additional held-out answer evaluations. For single-draw optimum mass u, the probability of seeing an optimum in S draws is 1-(1-u)^S. We compute this directly from the trained ideal statevector distribution and enumerate feasible energies. This calculation does not estimate a physical device's output distribution.

Means average seeds within question first. Conditional gaps describe the best feasible sample given that at least one is drawn; no-feasible probabilities and paired question intervals are also released. This development diagnostic compares final draws only: QAOA additionally performs angle training with up to 64 exact-expectation evaluations, whereas uniform feasible sampling does not. The same 20 questions recur across sizes, so the four size groups are not independent replications.

deep.label: Claim-to-artifact map
deep.html:
Claims and their evidence

This map distinguishes measured findings, mathematical properties and work that remains unverified. It is a review aid, not an independent validation certificate.

Statement Evidence Boundary
53,230 records in 24 complete conditions were audited Final audit, result index Includes 50,290 primary records and separately scoped controls, not 53,230 independent questions
The evidence-guided half-edge benefit is not established HotpotQA, MuSiQue Paired differences -0.0363 and -0.0095; both intervals cross zero. Equality/noninferiority is not established either
Prepared circuits do not establish a consistent guidance gain Prepared HotpotQA, prepared MuSiQue Post-freeze exploratory controls; both guidance intervals cross zero
Lower common objective energy can accompany worse answers Error signatures and examples, JSON Observations, not independent causal annotations; relevance is rescored with the same full coefficients
A first diagonal cost layer on a basis state is global phase Derivation, actual probability regression Mathematical limitation of this ansatz; not a new theorem about all QAOA implementations
Squared cardinality penalties add all-pairs couplings Quantum implementation, resource tables Complete costs are compiler-policy measurements; not proven minimum gate requirements
Uniform feasible sampling is strong at n=10,k=5 Sampling table, numerical evidence 1,024 draws cover one unique optimum with probability about 0.9829; QAOA additionally has angle-training cost
MILP linearization handles both coefficient signs Baseline tests, budget tests Numerical solver certification; larger time-limited cases are not all optimal
Sparse coefficients obey the stated absolute-error bound Derivation, checks No answer-quality guarantee follows from the coefficient bound
Embedding inputs are token-safe and persistent state is checked Retrieval tests, GPU input-length/profile evidence Mean pooling still approximates facts; tested workload is not every possible input
Corpus studies use shared retrieved pools Corpus manifest, restorer Closed union of benchmark inputs; not full Wikipedia or a deployed enterprise corpus
Public statistics and solver cases reconstruct Table reconstruction script, solver smoke evidence Different from rerunning full retrieval and LLM generation
The local API executes real inference and preserves state Service benchmark, recreated-container verification Five repeated fictional comparisons; no production SLA, browser visual approval or prompt-injection guarantee
The PDF was reviewed visually Export QA, PDF All 13 pages inspected for layout; no scientific peer-review claim

Not established: quantum advantage, physical-device performance, a verified factual knowledge graph, general evidence-preservation guarantees, exhaustive novelty, an original-model reproduction of the closest external selectors, independent semantic annotation, publication submission or acceptance. The literature matrix, limitations and handoff make these boundaries explicit.

questions: A sparse method uses fewer gates and its F1 interval crosses zero. Can we claim preserved answer quality?
No. A nonsignificant difference does not establish noninferiority. Also check that the circuit resource comparison includes all operations and uses an appropriate implementation.
chapters.html:
Begin with the denominator

The primary matrix contains 18 conditions and 50,290 method/question evaluations over 1,000 distinct held-out questions. Six scoped controls bring the total to 24 runs and 53,230 records: 53,209 successful and 21 failed. Main classical count comparisons use 500 questions per dataset/generator. Main quantum comparisons use 50 per dataset, at most ten candidates and three averaged seeds.

Four findings to carry forward

Lexical coverage has the highest observed F1 in all four main classical count settings. That is an observed ranking, not a universal superiority theorem.

Evidence-guided half-edge sparsification does not establish a benefit. Evidence-minus-magnitude differences are −0.0363 F1 on HotpotQA and −0.0095 on MuSiQue; both paired intervals cross zero. Prepared controls also fail to establish a consistent benefit.

Constraint encoding changes resources. A squared count penalty introduces all-pairs couplings. XY count preservation avoids that particular penalty but adds mixer/preparation costs. Generic synthetic-line compilation is not a minimum-gate proof or a physical timing measurement. The known-basis first cost layer can be redundant; state-aware simplification remains a review concern.

Lower energy can accompany worse answers. Full MILP has lower common-objective energy but worse F1 than relevance ranking on 31, 37, 36 and 32 questions across the four main count conditions. This is an observed proxy mismatch, not independent causal annotation of graph or generator errors.

Comparisons that must stay separate

The 1,200-token conditions use 100 questions, while count conditions use 500. The 25-candidate corpus studies use 100 questions; 50/100-candidate studies use 30. Their raw means do not isolate a causal effect across different populations. Larger one-second MILPs are not all certified optimal. Larger quantum sensitivities are only five MuSiQue questions per size.

Failures and output limits

One main penalty run produced no feasible sample. Twenty gate-cap diagnostic records could not satisfy the imposed cap; these remain failures. The audit flags 914 successful records reaching the 32-new-token generation allowance, which indicates possible truncation rather than proving every answer is incomplete. These are records, not distinct neural calls.

chapters.title: Follow the evidence
chapters.subtitle: A number should have a traceable path.
chapters.lead: Connect configuration, exact inputs, recorded outcomes, statistical reconstruction and the scientific claim.
chapters.body:
### Three levels of reproduction
1. **Rebuild saved tables:** read public compact predictions and recompute statistics. No model weights or raw passages are needed.
2. **Rerun fixed solver instances:** load frozen coefficients/constraints, execute MILP or simulated QAOA, and compare selections, energies and compiled costs. The bundle contains 110 instances.
3. **Rerun end-to-end inference:** restore datasets, model revisions and configurations; rebuild representations and generate answers. This is a different and more expensive check.

### The recorded chain
A configuration declares intended settings. A manifest adds input hashes, software, model revisions, IDs and backend information. An append-only journal records attempts and protects successful outcomes during resume. Summaries and paired intervals derive from those records; the manuscript assembler fills named numerical blocks.

SHA-256 identifies bytes; it does not establish that the bytes are scientifically correct. Seeds improve repeatability; they do not prevent leakage or guarantee identical kernels across machines. A source snapshot archives the calculation, whereas a hash alone does not.

### Try the model-free checks
These commands are optional hands-on verification; understanding the results does not require leaving this website.

~~~bash
venv/bin/python scripts/reproduce_public_tables.py --verify
venv/bin/python scripts/reproduce_quantum_instance.py --verify-recorded
~~~

The full in-site references include installation choices, exact input restoration and inference commands. The CPU container, CI and CUDA laptop have separate recorded environments. Automated reconstruction and a human independently reviewing the science are different checks.

deep.label: Complete reproduction guide
deep.html:
Reproduce the study and inspect its artifacts

The project offers two different checks: regenerate statistics from saved predictions, or repeat model/solver inference from restored inputs. The first is inexpensive and does not validate model behavior independently. The second needs the recorded weights, data and compute. Keep that distinction when reporting reproduction.

Environments

The measured research host uses Linux x86-64, Python 3.14, an RTX 5060 Laptop GPU with approximately 7.53 GiB of PyTorch-visible memory, and about 22 GiB host RAM. The two generators fit sequentially; do not load both alongside competing GPU jobs. Models run in inference mode, without fine-tuning or a paid API.

  • requirements-laptop.lock: exact observed host environment, including CUDA-specific wheels. It is not a portable CPU installation recipe. CUDA Torch is fetched from its matching official PyTorch index.
  • requirements-ci.txt: the lighter tested correctness/lint/build environment without model downloads.
  • requirements-container.lock: observed CPU demonstration environment; CPU Torch is installed separately from the official CPU index by Dockerfile.
  • requirements-baselines.lock: small historical NumPy/SciPy baseline environment.

For a fresh CPU correctness environment:

python3.14 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-ci.txt
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --no-deps .
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

The full CI environment includes Qiskit and exercises the actual circuit tests. The minimal baseline environment explicitly skips unavailable optional integrations. No fake backend is used for scientific results; test doubles are confined to orchestration/service tests.

Restore exact inputs

From a fresh working tree with the research dependencies installed:

venv/bin/python -m pip install -e '.[models,research,service,dev,publishing]'
venv/bin/python scripts/download_models.py
venv/bin/python scripts/restore_splits.py
venv/bin/python scripts/restore_corpus_candidates.py

The extras command resolves dependencies and is a convenience installation, not an exact environment recreation. Use the tested environment snapshots for exact versions. Model revisions and every final configuration fix immutable snapshots. Download scripts obtain public artifacts from their original hosts; they do not enable remote model code. The MuSiQue archive is approximately 272 MB, and all weights/data require additional disk space. There is no cloud or QPU prerequisite.

The split restorer checks the official MuSiQue archive hash and reconstructs rows in frozen ID order from pinned HotpotQA sources and the official MuSiQue archive. Existing different files are rejected. The corpus restorer uses saved retrieved IDs and profile values to reconstruct the six exact candidate files without rerunning embedding search. All four split and six corpus-file hashes were independently reconstructed during this run.

Restoring frozen candidate files verifies selection inputs. To rerun candidate retrieval itself, prepare_corpus_experiment.py builds checked FAISS/SQLite indexes and records dense/BM25 rank-fusion profiles. It is a separate expensive operation and can expose numeric/platform ordering differences; never silently replace frozen pools in a primary solver comparison.

Full inference

The protocol explains principal comparisons, failure policy and changes. The primary matrix checks each configuration's SHA-256 before starting sequential runs:

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false \
  venv/bin/python scripts/run_matrix.py --matrix configs/final_matrix.json
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false \
  venv/bin/python scripts/complete_evaluation.py

The completion driver requires all 18 primary conditions to be complete, then runs the formulation control, complete-gate-cap diagnostic, exploratory preparation control, artifact audits and assembly. --wait-for-primary is for a separately running primary controller; do not launch duplicate controllers or writers. Per-run logs are under the ignored root results directory. It can be normal for a completed scientific run to contain explicit failures; a successful process exit alone is insufficient to establish a complete question/method grid.

Primary records total 50,290 method/question evaluations over 1,000 distinct held-out questions. Repeated methods, seeds and generator conditions are not additional independent questions. Secondary controls have separate manifests and sample sizes. Exact-expectation simulator training, finite-shot training and artificial final-sampling noise have different resource meanings.

The preparation extension has its own source snapshot and composite identity because it changes the circuit without changing the frozen primary core. It is post-freeze exploratory. The original basis-start circuit and Unicode-provenance cycle-one archive are retained and clearly distinguished from definitive cycle two.

For an independent rerun alongside existing outputs, use a fresh checkout/output tree. Never delete existing scientific artifacts to make resume accept changed settings. Resume requires matching code/config/data/environment identities and protects successful results. Single-condition commands are available through python -m qrag.experiments.study --help; a new result directory is the safest choice when changing an experiment.

Saved-prediction reconstruction

After final evidence is exported:

venv/bin/python scripts/reproduce_public_tables.py --verify

This verifies compressed-prediction hashes and regenerates method tables and paired intervals without model weights or dataset text.

The released optimization fixture manifest additionally identifies 110 fixed coefficient arrays. To reproduce original, prepared or sparse solver cases without an encoder or LLM:

venv/bin/python scripts/reproduce_quantum_instance.py --verify-recorded
venv/bin/python scripts/reproduce_quantum_instance.py --prepared --verify-recorded
venv/bin/python scripts/reproduce_quantum_instance.py \
  --run final_musique_quantum --sparsifier evidence --verify-recorded

The first frozen question is used unless an ID is supplied. The command checks the fixture hash and frozen source identity, runs actual Qiskit and MILP, and can compare selected indices, full energy and compiled gates with the recorded case. Exact recorded checks were verified in the pinned laptop environment; seeds and version pins do not guarantee identical variational trajectories on arbitrary machines. The normal result records still expose feasibility, energies and resources when exact verification is not requested.

For full local result assembly, use:

venv/bin/python scripts/audit_final_runs.py
venv/bin/python scripts/error_analysis.py
venv/bin/python scripts/assemble_results.py
venv/bin/python scripts/analyze_sampling_coverage.py
venv/bin/python scripts/build_architecture_figure.py
venv/bin/python scripts/export_quantum_instances.py
venv/bin/python scripts/reproduce_public_tables.py --verify
venv/bin/python scripts/build_paper_pdf.py

The auditor uses local full artifacts and pinned tokenizers. It recomputes scores, selected source membership, objective/surrogate energies, budgets and exact prompt token IDs. The report assembler requires complete grids and retains failed questions as zero answer scores. Completed zero-feasible circuits remain in circuit feasibility/resource means; unmeasured resources are not invented zeros. The sampling analyzer reads its saved development-only numerical evidence.

PDF rendering uses ReportLab with system Liberation Serif fonts and Matplotlib equation rendering. The final export must also be rendered and visually inspected with Poppler; a successful PDF write alone is not visual QA. See the manuscript's accompanying evidence for the actual completed checks rather than inferring success from available commands.

What is public and what remains local

Public: implementation, configurations, frozen IDs/hashes, compact question-level predictions, statistics, figures, manuscript source, documentation and CI. Local: raw/processed data, weights, caches, large full predictions with source text/prompts/input IDs, superseded execution archives and temporary document renders. The rights boundary is documented in attribution.

Compact exports preserve the hashes of original local artifacts. Their availability does not mean every large original file is included in Git. Restorers and the frozen source/configurations support the full inference route. Git commit identity, code snapshots and recorded runtime settings should accompany any later reproduction or revised experiment.

The versioned artifact builder requires a clean committed working tree and an already built wheel. venv/bin/python scripts/build_release_bundle.py checks public evidence/PDF identities, archives only tracked source material and creates checksums under the ignored local release directory. It excludes private notes, raw/processed data and weights. See the handoff for rights-holder and submission decisions that remain outside the local run.

deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Reproducibility and software contracts

Configuration and package installation

config.py loads TOML into ExperimentConfig and rejects unknown keys. post_init checks types, numeric ranges, finite weights, device choices and immutable model revisions. Explicit type checks prevent boolean values from accidentally serving as positive integers.

The larger study uses JSON specifications in study.py. Its validate_spec rejects unknown top-level settings, validates the model through ExperimentConfig, checks method-name uniqueness, solver names, budget mode and selected limits. Per-method dictionaries do not have a comprehensive unknown-key/type validator. It would be inaccurate to claim that every malformed nested study setting is rejected before execution. Frozen configurations and correctness checks reduce this risk but do not remove that interface limitation. The service separately uses strict Pydantic request models.

The package configuration in pyproject.toml makes qrag importable. An editable installation points imports at the source tree. Installing the package does not download model weights.

requirements-baselines.lock pins the small historical core. requirements-laptop.lock records the tested laptop environment, including transitive packages, while requirements-ci.txt pins the lighter CI environment. The CUDA laptop snapshot is host-specific, not a guarantee of portable installation on every platform. Model snapshot revisions identify weights/configuration; package pins identify software. Both matter. pip documentation

Manifest versus configuration

A configuration states what is requested. A manifest records that configuration together with dataset/source identities, actual backend, package versions, selected question IDs, preparation and execution details.

The runner seeds Python, NumPy and PyTorch in the real backend. Seeds do not repair dataset leakage, ensure correct metrics or guarantee identical floating-point results on every platform.

SHA-256 maps file bytes to an identifying digest. A changed dataset produces a different expected identity even if the filename stays the same. The package source hash covers qrag Python files. Main-study outputs also save their exact source snapshot; the hash alone would not archive the bytes or external dependencies. Git metadata and model revisions add context but are not substitutes for preserving source and data.

Atomic files and resume

artifacts.py writes a temporary file in the target directory, flushes it, calls fsync and replaces the destination. This reduces the risk of a visibly half-written JSON artifact. It is not a multi-file database transaction, concurrent-writer protocol or complete guarantee against every power-loss scenario.

RunStore keys each prediction by question ID and method. Duplicate keys are rejected. Resume checks configuration, dataset, question IDs, source, environment and backend identity before reusing records.

The historical RunStore skips recorded successes and errors. The later study runner uses JournalRunStore in journal.py: it appends and fsyncs each record, protects successful keys, records explicit attempts for retried errors, and saves a torn final line before recovery. Resume checks scientific identity first. Final reporting takes the latest attempt for each key; the append history remains inspectable. Runs have one writer; this journal is not a distributed database or a multiwriter locking protocol.

Per-method failures after startup are recorded and retained in the answer denominator. Exceptions during model preparation produce failure artifacts after the store exists. Configuration, dataset loading or snapshot-resolution errors occurring before store creation may only produce a CLI error. This is an implementation boundary, not an assurance that every failure has a manifest.

Tests and their limits

The first seventeen tests covered the baseline. The expanded suite has 46 tests covering data, caches/indexes, provenance, signed MILP, budgets, quantum spectra and mixers, sparsification, statistics, journaling and service behavior. Several methods contain multiple cases. Run the suite with venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q; an explicit test directory avoids discovering the separately extracted release copy under ignored local results.

Orchestration and service tests use explicitly labeled fake inference engines; numerical and quantum tests execute their actual solver/circuit dependencies. These tests do not measure language-model quality. The historical MiniLM/Qwen run verified three development examples; the later real-model experiments and CPU-container checks provide the broader integration evidence.

The baseline workflow and the expanded research workflow have completed successfully on GitHub Actions. These checks do not download model weights or reproduce full scientific inference; local real-model runs provide that separate evidence. Container and wheel checks exercise packaging as well as Python tests.
