deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Sparsification changes the optimization problem

Let the sparse objective retain pair terms through a mask Mᵢⱼ:

E~(x)=∑iaixi+∑i<jMijbijxixj.\widetilde E(x)=\sum_i a_i x_i+\sum_{i<j}M_{ij}b_{ij}x_i x_j.E(x)=i∑​ai​xi​+i<j∑​Mij​bij​xi​xj​.

Both classical and quantum solvers must be evaluated against the original target as well as the surrogate. Otherwise a lower reported energy may merely reflect removal of costs.

Let R be the removed edge set and let δ be the sum of |bᵢⱼ| over R. Every binary product xᵢxⱼ is zero or one. The magnitude of each removed term is therefore at most |bᵢⱼ|, and the triangle inequality bounds their sum:

∣E(x)−E~(x)∣≤δ.|E(x)-\widetilde E(x)|\le\delta.∣E(x)−E(x)∣≤δ.

If both problems have the same feasible set and the sparse solution is ε-suboptimal under the sparse objective, then:

E(x~)≤E~(x~)+δ≤E~(x⋆)+ϵ+δ≤E(x⋆)+ϵ+2δ.E(\widetilde x) \le\widetilde E(\widetilde x)+\delta \le\widetilde E(x^\star)+\epsilon+\delta \le E(x^\star)+\epsilon+2\delta.E(x)≤E(x)+δ≤E(x⋆)+ϵ+δ≤E(x⋆)+ϵ+2δ.

Read the chain one step at a time. First replace the full energy of the sparse solution by its sparse energy plus δ. Second use ε-suboptimality: the chosen sparse solution is no worse than any feasible comparison, including the full optimum, plus ε. Third replace that comparison's sparse energy by its full energy plus δ. Rearranging gives a full-objective gap of at most 2δ+ε.

The feasible set, candidates, budgets, coefficient scale and energy offsets must be the same in both problems. This elementary bound can be loose; it is a sanity check, not a new theorem or an answer-F1 guarantee. A sampled QAOA selection has no known ε certificate unless a separate solver optimum or bound establishes its sparse-objective gap.

Circuit resources must include state preparation, mixers, routing and constraint encoding. Sparsifying interactions generally does not reduce the number of candidate qubits. A statevector simulator stores amplitudes growing as 2ⁿ; raw complex128 storage alone is about 16 × 2ⁿ bytes, before additional simulator memory. Simulation behavior cannot establish practical hardware speedup.

deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Phase F foundations — exact edge budgets and what sparsification can prove

The four rules

Take the nonzero upper-triangular interactions as unordered edges. If there are m edges and retained fraction f, keep floor(f*m) edges exactly. Absolute retention sorts by |b_ij|. Random retention uses a recorded seeded permutation. The degree rule ranks each edge in each endpoint's incident list, takes the smaller endpoint rank as its symmetric priority, then breaks ties by magnitude and indices until the same hard budget is filled. It is a degree-oriented heuristic, not a guaranteed degree-regular graph.

Evidence guidance ranks linked pairs by C_ij*sqrt(|b_ij|), protects at most ceil(budget/2) such edges, and fills remaining slots from the absolute ordering. When there are too many bridge candidates, only the highest-ranked fit. When none exist, the rule reduces to magnitude retention. Both positive and negative retained coefficients are unchanged. All linear relevance terms remain. The method can protect mistaken links; the graph's name is not a preservation guarantee.

Step-by-step objective bound

The complete three-step proof and its assumptions are in Sparsification changes the optimization problem. The implementation computes delta from the absolute mass of removed signed coefficients and reports both full and surrogate energies. This connects the recorded masks to the bound without assuming that QAOA has a certified epsilon or that an energy bound controls answer F1.

Why a random control matters for small quantum cases

A best-of-many-shot policy also evaluates many candidate subsets classically. The uniform feasible-sampling control uses the same final draw count and a recorded seed, rather than comparing QAOA with one arbitrary subset. The combinatorial derivation, 10/16-candidate examples and distinction between equal final draws and equal total compute are explained together in How repeated samples can look like optimization. That derivation is the reason this control was added before the final comparisons.

Calibrating without reusing the test set

For each candidate gamma, compute development mean F1 separately on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, average those two means with equal weight, and choose the highest score; ties favor smaller gamma. The selected value is 0.2. Unequal candidate-pool sizes do not give MuSiQue extra weight under this rule. Development tuning makes those development estimates optimistic. Only the frozen held-out evaluation can test whether the choice transfers. The main edge fraction remains the predeclared 0.5, with 0.25/0.75 as secondary sensitivity settings.

Durable progress and repeated seeds

Appending one JSON record and flushing it avoids rewriting a growing file after each result. Fsync asks the operating system to commit the write. A crash can still interrupt the final line. Resume checks the immutable identity first, retains incomplete tail bytes for audit, then recomputes that unfinished record. Error retries get incremented attempt numbers; successful records cannot be replaced. Analysis uses the latest validated attempt for each question/method.

Repeated seeds describe solver variability on one question. For a method with three seeds, average its three F1 values inside that question, counting failures as zero, then bootstrap question means. Treating those three seeds as three unrelated questions would inflate the apparent sample size. The confidence intervals describe sampling variation over the observed question population and do not account for unknown pretrained-model contamination or every modeling choice.

deep.label: Measured results and boundaries
deep.html:
Phase F — calibrated weights, sparsification and research decision

A development-only sweep used 100 questions per dataset and gamma in {0,0.1,0.2,0.4,0.8}. Gamma=0.2 maximized the unweighted mean answer F1 across the two development datasets; the decision and all scores are recorded. HotpotQA base/selected-weight F1 is 0.6358/0.6533; MuSiQue is 0.1868/0.2205. These are tuned development results, not held-out gains. Greedy lexical coverage remains a strong comparator. The earlier gamma=0.8 negative result is not removed.

Implemented exact unordered-edge budgets for absolute magnitude, seeded random, endpoint-degree ranking and evidence-guided protection. Evidence guidance reserves up to half the hard edge budget, rounded upward, for high-priority possible bridges and fills the rest by coefficient magnitude. It never silently exceeds the total budget, even if more links are candidates for protection. Retained coefficients keep their signs. Every solution is scored under both its sparse surrogate and the original full objective.

The 30-question development ablation contains 900 successful records. Full graph MILP mean F1 is 0.6203; full XY-QAOA is 0.5634; uniform best-of-1,024 feasible samples is 0.6203. At half edges, QAOA absolute and evidence-guided selection both score 0.4834; the corresponding sparse MILPs score 0.4491 and 0.4891. Small-sample/tuning limitations prevent a general ranking claim.

Mean line two-qubit gates fall from 263.87 for full XY-QAOA to 176.43 for absolute and 176.63 for evidence-guided half-edge variants. The half-edge penalty variants both have 45 encoded pairs and 199 mean line gates. Thus edge removal does reduce complete compiled cost in one encoding while the penalty can erase structural savings. It does not establish preserved answer quality.

Research decision: continue as an encoding-aware comparative study rather than promise a positive evidence-preservation result. The analysis retains paired uncertainty. Add uniform feasible sampling to final comparisons because best-of-many measurements can cover much of a small feasible space. No quantum advantage is inferred from finding a good subset after many classical energy evaluations.

The study runner now uses an append/fsync journal with explicit error retries and torn-tail recovery. Successful records cannot be overwritten; a changed resume identity fails before file mutation. Report generation groups repeated solver seeds within question before resampling. Thirty-eight offline tests pass. A reconstruction check rebuilt all four frozen dataset files in a separate directory and matched their exact hashes.

deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Reading statistical comparisons correctly

For question q, let d_q be method A's F1 minus method B's F1 after averaging each method's seeds. The estimated difference is the arithmetic mean of d_q across the N common questions. A paired bootstrap samples N question IDs with replacement, recomputes that mean, and repeats 10,000 times. The 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles give the reported 95% interval. Pairing preserves the fact that both methods face the same easy or difficult question.

If three seeds on one question score 1, 0.5 and 0, that question contributes 0.5. It does not become three independently sampled questions. If the last seed fails, its F1 remains zero and the mean is still 0.5. In contrast, missing resource measurements remain missing: inventing a gate count of zero for an unexecuted circuit would also bias a resource mean. Completed circuits with measured zero feasibility do contribute their actual zero.

An interval entirely above zero supports a positive difference under this sample and analysis. An interval spanning zero leaves both positive and negative effects plausible. It does not establish that the methods are equal. Noninferiority would require a chosen acceptable loss and a suitable interval bound declared before looking at the result. This project does not retrospectively invent such a tolerance.

The question is the resampling unit, but source passages and compositional question templates can still be shared across questions. The bootstrap does not model every such cluster. The two generators are from one family, and numerical simulator training is not physical-device execution. These limits restrict generalization even when a difference looks clear. Secondary exploratory tables are not a large collection of independent confirmatory discoveries.

deep.label: Measured results and boundaries
deep.html:
Phase G — definitive evaluation and independent audit

The 18-condition definitive primary matrix is complete: 50,290 method/question evaluations over 1,000 distinct held-out questions. Separate controls add 800 formulation, 140 gate-cap and 2,000 prepared-circuit records, giving 53,230 records across 24 completed runs. All 24 grids were audited. The primary and formulation runs share the same frozen core source fingerprint; the preparation control adds an explicitly hashed extension. Documentation and service commits changed during execution, so a common scientific source hash is more precise than claiming one repository commit for every run.

The audit recomputed dataset-specific scores, checked IDs/counts/token budgets, summed full and sparse energies independently, verified source/config/data identities and retokenized saved prompts. It independently counted feasible shots from measured bit strings, including failed circuits. The gate diagnostic's retained masks and final complete line circuits were reconstructed and recompiled. Its successful circuits satisfy the 180-gate cap. Audit evidence records every checked condition.

There is one genuine no-feasible-sample failure in the primary matrix: HotpotQA question 5add9bfa5542990dbb2f7e85, penalty-full seed 42. It remains zero in answer averages and zero in completed-circuit feasibility. Twenty additional gate-cap control records reject the penalty encoding because no tested retention level fits the cap; they are explicit diagnostic failures rather than successful substituted executions. No service fallback enters scientific results.

Findings and interpretation

The principal half-edge comparison does not establish an evidence-guidance benefit on either dataset. Both intervals include zero, so neither equality nor noninferiority follows. Lexical coverage has the highest observed F1 in all four 500-question classical count conditions. Graph-minus-base effects vary across settings and their reported exploratory intervals also include zero. These results support a bounded comparative/negative-result account, not a new state-of-the-art or quantum-advantage claim.

The one-second MILP setting can return feasible incumbents without an optimality certificate. Larger-pool results do not demonstrate quantum scaling.

Objective quality is not answer quality

Across the four 500-question fixed-count conditions, full MILP has lower common-objective energy but worse F1 than relevance selection on respectively 31, 37, 36, 32 questions (HotpotQA 1.5B/3B, MuSiQue 1.5B/3B). The relevance subset is rescored using the full MILP coefficients for this comparison. These observations directly distinguish proxy optimization from downstream correctness; they do not independently identify a causal graph or generator error. Deterministic examples and additional signatures are released.

Complete result index

Each linked analysis includes every method in that condition, answer/evidence/token outcomes, failures and paired intervals. Its JSON companion additionally retains resource and certification diagnostics. The public compact prediction file is identified and checksummed by the matching evidence manifest.

What can be reproduced without a model

All 24 public prediction tables and their paired intervals reconstruct without loading an LLM or raw dataset. An additional 110-instance coefficient bundle supports solver-only experiments over 100 distinct quantum-subset questions and nested 12/16-candidate sensitivities. It contains no answer/support labels or source text. Four actual solver reproductions match recorded selected indices, full energy and compiled line gates: original full XY, prepared full XY, evidence-sparse XY and a 16-candidate case. Reproduction checks document the scope.

The exact core source snapshot and preparation extension snapshots are released alongside configurations. Full prompts/input IDs remain in the large local run bundles; public restorers rebuild the frozen inputs from primary hosts. Model-free table regeneration is not an independent rerun of answer generation.

The error-signature analysis includes deterministic examples of better common objective values with worse answers. These observations explain why optimizing a proxy does not certify useful evidence. They are not independently annotated causal error labels. Source overlap, imperfect references, weak entity links, a small quantum subset, one generator family and ideal statevector training remain limits.

deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Connecting the completed results to the mathematics

The principal evidence-minus-magnitude differences are -0.0363 and -0.0095 F1, with intervals that cross zero. This does not prove that entity links are always useless. It says this extractor, scoring rule, sparsifier, shallow circuit, candidate pool and sample do not establish the proposed benefit. A weak feature, limited statistical precision and an optimization restriction can all matter; the current experiment does not independently identify their causal shares.

The prepared control removes the specific global-phase degeneracy, but its two evidence-guidance intervals still cross zero. An improvement in expressivity is a mathematical property; an improvement in answer F1 is an empirical property. They must be measured separately. The full report retains both controls rather than replacing one after seeing scores.

For a complete optimum, E(x*) <= E(x) for every feasible x under that coefficient array. This inequality contains no reference answer, supporting annotation or LLM likelihood. It therefore cannot imply that the generated answer is correct. The released error analysis demonstrates real cases of lower common energy and lower answer F1. It evaluates the relevance subset using the same full coefficients, avoiding the invalid comparison of energies from different graph weights.

A 1,200-token cap bounds formatted context but leaves room for different consumption and selected counts. Comparing it with a 500-question count result would additionally change the question population, since the token condition has 100 questions. Within-condition paired comparisons are interpretable; a raw cross-table difference does not isolate the effect of the cap. Larger candidate pools similarly change retrieval opportunities and optimization cost together.

The gate-cap diagnostic uses descending recorded floating-point fractions and an integer floor edge budget. Near a floating-point boundary, a value represented as 0.3999999999999999 can retain 17 of 45 edges rather than the 18 associated with an exact decimal 0.4. The artifact records the actual fraction, retained indices, trial costs and final circuit. The principal 0.5 fractions are exactly representable and unaffected. Final cap validation, not a rounded display label, establishes feasibility. Compiled gate cost is not monotonic in retained edges because routing and optimization can change.

The service measures an entire three-method comparison request, not a single generated token or one selector in isolation. Its p95 comes from only five repeated fictional requests. Batching measurements use synchronized GPU embedding operations on 128 fixed chunks; their scope differs from both the CPU service and dataset evaluation. An engineering number becomes useful when its workload, denominator, warm/cold state and resource conditions are explicit.

The 110 frozen optimization instances allow Qiskit/MILP experiments without loading an embedding model, raw dataset or generator. Reference solver optima in that bundle are analysis outputs, not answer annotations. The reproduction command passes only coefficients and constraints to the solver, then compares its output against the stored execution. Reconstructing saved statistical tables, rerunning a solver on fixed features, and rerunning end-to-end RAG are three different levels of reproduction.

phases.title: H · Service, profiles and manuscript
phases.why: Research code must be inspectable, restartable and explainable. A working interface is useful, but must not manufacture scientific claims.
phases.how: Added FastAPI jobs, strict inputs, durable queue state, explicit fallback, tracing and a separate local dashboard. Checked actual CPU inference and restart persistence, profiled synchronized GPU embedding batches, assembled and visually reviewed a 13-page manuscript.
phases.math: Reported percentiles and throughput need denominators and workloads. GPU batching amortizes overhead, subject to memory. Five fictional service comparisons are not a production latency benchmark.
phases.result: The service uses the same research library and real local models. Saved outputs survive container recreation with their named state volume. The manuscript numerical sections derive from artifacts.
phases.boundary: No production deployment or prompt-injection guarantee is established. Continuous generation batching, a demo video and independent causal error annotation are absent. The guided website is a later presentation layer, not a new scientific run.

deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Service foundations — requests, jobs and observability

An HTTP API is a contract through which clients request operations. FastAPI validates JSON against typed Pydantic schemas. Unknown answer/relevance fields are rejected rather than quietly entering inference. A valid request receives status 202 and a job ID: accepted does not mean completed. The client polls that ID until the job completes or reports a failure. Invalid input receives 422; a full bounded queue receives 429; readiness returns 503 while model weights are not ready. Health and readiness answer different operational questions.

The inference worker runs outside the HTTP event loop, so a long model call does not block every health request. There is one inference worker and at most four accepted outstanding jobs. This prevents unbounded memory growth and overlapping model calls on one GPU. An exclusive database lock rejects accidental second workers using the same store. SQLite transactions persist job state; after restart, abandoned queued/running jobs are marked interrupted instead of being falsely reported complete. Terminal job retention is bounded.

Concurrency means multiple requests can be in progress; parallelism means computations actually execute simultaneously. Increasing web workers can duplicate model weights and exhaust memory. The service therefore serializes inference while still allowing request validation and status polling. Chunk embedding batches many texts into one model operation; that is different from launching concurrent generator requests.

Deadlines are checked between bounded stages. Generation has an output-token bound, solvers have evaluation/time budgets and inputs have size limits. These are not preemptive hard wall-clock cancellation: an already running tensor operation is not forcibly killed. A deadline failure is recorded. A quantum selection failure may trigger a separately labeled MILP fallback if the request permits it. The requested and actual methods, reason and resource fields remain visible. Research evaluation never substitutes that service fallback into QAOA results.

A trace groups stage spans under one request. Spans measure preparation, embedding, graph construction, selection and generation; structured logs identify job completion/failure without logging source text. OpenTelemetry can export local console spans. Queue time is start minus acceptance time; service time is completion minus start; total latency includes both. The operational p50 is the median of retained completed jobs, while p95 is the value below approximately 95% of that measured population. Mixed ingestion/query jobs and cold starts must not be confused with a homogeneous warm-query latency target. No unmeasured service-level promise is made.

Persistent corpus ingestion stores a checked FAISS/SQLite bundle through the same library used in experiments. Query requests retrieve candidates, then use the common selector and generator. Corpus IDs are constrained to simple names rather than arbitrary filesystem paths. This service is a local demonstration; its inference inputs contain no reference answers.

deep.label: Measured results and boundaries
deep.html:
Phase H — actual service, persistence and batching measurements

The locked nonroot CPU container completed real model ingestion and inference. Cold ingestion including preparation took 10.48 seconds. Five model-ready fictional requests each compared relevance, MILP and simulated QAOA; all three returned India. Their measured comparison-request p50/p95 were 2.108/2.441 seconds. These are five repeated requests on one fictional workload, not dataset accuracy, isolated production throughput or a latency guarantee. CPU artifact audits ran during parts of these integration checks.

Document/query embedding cache hits increased across requests, and graph cache hits appeared after the first identical comparison. A persistent corpus query returned four candidates and completed generation. The container was then recreated with the same named state volume: a completed job's full response remained exactly equal, cold readiness returned again, and the stored corpus successfully answered another query after model preparation. Actual local stage spans were captured. Service measurements and operational verification retain the details.

The untrusted-source input fixture returned India, but the selector supplied only the two normal evidence sources. It therefore does not test whether the generator resists an instruction that actually reaches its context. No prompt-injection resistance is claimed. Browser surfaces were unavailable, so HTTP/static checks are complete but visual dashboard review remains external.

GPU embedding batches

A separate model-ready profile encoded the same 128 development chunks, with maximum input length 240 tokens, at batch sizes 1/8/32/64. It used three randomized-order repeats, CUDA synchronization and vector-agreement checks. It did not batch generation or alter research settings. The first timing export is retained locally; the final export additionally verifies the input-length bound.

Batch Median chunks/second Peak allocated GPU bytes
1 501.5 129,467,904
8 1018.2 160,437,248
32 1152.3 256,458,240
64 989.6 387,993,088

Batch 32 processes about 2.30 times as many chunks per second as batch 1 on this workload, with higher allocated memory. Batch 64 is slower than 32 here and uses more memory. This illustrates a measured throughput/memory tradeoff rather than a rule that larger batches always improve speed. Profile evidence records all twelve measurements.

The service has strict input schemas, one inference worker, a four-job bound, persisted statuses, explicit fallbacks, source provenance and local tracing. It is a loopback demonstration without authentication or a production reliability claim. Forty-six correctness tests, targeted type checks, wheel/container checks and both current GitHub CI workflows pass.

deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Turning numerical artifacts into a manuscript

The report assembler reads completed per-question outcomes, derives statistics and fills only named numerical blocks in the manuscript. This keeps the explanation editable while avoiding hand-transcribed table values. The PDF renderer typesets equations, tables and generated figures from that source. A successful rendering process can still produce clipped labels, split captions or unreadable columns, so each of the 13 pages was separately rasterized and visually inspected.

An export checksum identifies the reviewed PDF bytes. It does not establish that the research is correct or guarantee a bit-identical export with different fonts or rendering-library versions. Similarly, a polished PDF is not a submitted or accepted publication. Source review, author responsibility, venue requirements and independent evidence checking remain distinct from layout QA.

deep.label: Operational guide
deep.html:
Local demonstration and API

The service calls the same retrieval, graph, selection and generation library as the experiments. It accepts source text and questions, not reference answers. It is a local demonstration with serialized inference, not a production multiuser deployment. The live laboratory is served at /, the complete project walkthrough at /journey, and interactive OpenAPI documentation at /docs.

Complete project walkthrough

Open /journey to follow the problem, current state, original plan, foundations, research protocol, baseline and phases A–I, measured results, reproducibility, service and manuscript. Guided and deep modes include the full references inside the website. Search, a glossary, a phase explorer, numerical examples, saved-result charts and a literal JSON evidence viewer support the explanation. None of these controls submits inference jobs; model-cold readiness does not block reading.

The journey guide documents content sources, navigation, development-only dependencies and rebuilding. The compiled bundle, equations, fonts and figures ship with the Python package; no external JavaScript/font CDN or Node runtime is needed by visitors. The result explorer reads public saved analyses, while clearly labelled examples calculate illustrative quantities in the browser. Quantum execution remains simulated, and the original research conclusions remain unchanged.

Functional, numerical, HTTP and packaging checks are recorded separately from visual review in the journey verification receipt. The available browser connection failed before navigation; actual desktop/mobile painting and browser interaction review remain unverified.

Dashboard

The dashboard uses a paper background, a dotted grid, blue accents and local display/serif/monospace fonts, with visual inspiration from AI Engineering from Scratch. Its layout, diagram and application code are specific to Q-RAG. All fonts are served locally; their upstream license notices are in the font directory. The browser does not need an external font service.

Edit source titles and text in Cards mode, or use JSON mode to edit the complete source array, including IDs. Add/remove sources, set the shared count, choose selectors and press Compare methods. Reset example restores the fictional demonstration. Arrow keys switch editor tabs. The interface exposes model-cold, queued, running, completed and failed states. Changing inputs after a result marks the displayed answers as belonging to the previous comparison.

Each result shows its actual answer, supplied sources, context tokens, selection/generation time, objective, solver status and any classical fallback. Expand the source details to read the context supplied to the generator. Expand QAOA details to see feasible shots and complete compiled line costs. The graph includes a text disclosure of shared entities, so inspecting a link does not depend on hovering. At most 16 graph nodes are drawn in a large pool; the interface discloses that limit and lists all extracted links.

The headline dataset/question/record counts describe the frozen research study. They are not live service counters. The hero diagram is labeled illustrative. No new evidence-guidance or quantum-advantage claim is introduced by the redesign.

The current laptop demonstration remains at http://127.0.0.1:8766/. The redesigned container reuses the existing named state volume and read-only model mount. The stopped qrag-release-demo-before-redesign container is retained for rollback; do not run both containers against the same job database. Standard source/container installation below builds the current dashboard as part of the service.

Frontend behavior checks

The small DOM check script runs application events with explicitly synthetic API responses. It needs Node and jsdom only for development verification; the dashboard itself has no Node build or runtime requirement.

npm install --prefix .cache/dashboard-checks --no-audit --no-fund jsdom@26.1.0
NODE_PATH="$PWD/.cache/dashboard-checks/node_modules" node scripts/check_dashboard.cjs
node --check src/qrag_service/static/dashboard.js
venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_service.py -q

The nine DOM checks cover source editing, JSON round trips, count limits, reset, validation, answer/source/circuit rendering, explicit fallback, text-only rendering of untrusted output, failure recovery and keyboard tabs. These checks do not render CSS or establish browser layout, accessibility certification or general injection resistance. The redesign verification separately records real HTTP/model execution, asset hashes and the remaining browser-review limit.

Run on the laptop

From the repository root with the tested environment and downloaded model snapshots:

venv/bin/python scripts/download_models.py --core-only
QRAG_TRACE_CONSOLE=1 venv/bin/uvicorn qrag_service.app:app \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --workers 1

The first job loads the frozen MiniLM and Qwen 1.5B snapshots. /health can succeed while /ready returns 503 because weights are not loaded. This is expected cold readiness, not a crashed application. The first job includes model preparation time. QRAG_DEVICE=cpu forces CPU; otherwise the local service uses CUDA when available. The GPU path uses float16 generation and the CPU path uses float32.

The service's qaoa option uses the frozen basis-start XY p=1 circuit. Its first cost phase is global; the prepared exploratory ansatz is currently a research control, not silently substituted into this API. See the state-preparation derivation.

Container

docker build -t qrag-research:local .
docker volume create qrag-service-state
docker run --rm --name qrag-demo -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
  --cpus=4 --memory=12g \
  -e QRAG_TRACE_CONSOLE=1 \
  --mount type=volume,src=qrag-service-state,dst=/app/.cache \
  --mount type=bind,src="$HOME/.cache/huggingface/hub",dst=/home/app/.cache/huggingface/hub,readonly \
  qrag-research:local

The image uses CPU PyTorch, runs as a nonroot user, contains no model weights and resolves models offline through the read-only mount. The named volume holds caches, indexes and job state. It is separate from the weight cache. The image build needs network access to public package repositories. WITH_MODELS=0 builds the lighter import/HTTP CI image; it cannot execute real model inference without the omitted packages.

The observed CPU runtime is pinned in requirements-container.lock; the lighter HTTP/tracing closure is in requirements-container-service.lock. CPU Torch is pinned separately and fetched from the official PyTorch CPU index. These CPU package versions differ from the CUDA research host, whose exact snapshot is requirements-laptop.lock. The container verifies service portability; it is not claimed to be a bit-identical GPU research environment.

Endpoints and meanings

Request Result
GET /journey Model-free project walkthrough with locally served references and saved results
GET /health Process can answer requests; states that quantum hardware is false
GET /ready 200 when models are ready; otherwise 503 with a cold-state description
POST /jobs Validate a supplied-pool comparison and return 202 with a job ID
GET /jobs/{id} Poll queued/running/completed/failed/timed_out/interrupted state and results
POST /corpora Submit persistent corpus ingestion as a bounded background job
POST /query Retrieve from an ingested corpus and compare selectors
GET /metrics JSON queue/job/timing counters, not a Prometheus text endpoint

An example comparison request is:

{
  "question": "In which country was the director of Film A born?",
  "sources": [
    {"id": "a", "title": "Film A", "text": "Film A was directed by Maya Rao."},
    {"id": "b", "title": "Maya Rao", "text": "Maya Rao was born in India."},
    {"id": "c", "title": "Film release", "text": "Film A was released in 1995."}
  ],
  "methods": ["relevance", "milp", "qaoa"],
  "k": 2,
  "allow_classical_fallback": true,
  "deadline_seconds": 120
}

The response's status_url identifies the polling endpoint. A 202 response means accepted, not successfully answered. Results include the requested and actual method, supplied source IDs, generated text, context/input/output tokens, stage costs and simulation resources. Supplied IDs identify the context given to the model; they do not prove the answer is supported by every listed source.

Corpus ingestion uses {"corpus":"demo","sources":[...]}. A subsequent query uses {"corpus":"demo","question":"...","candidates":20,"k":3,"retrieval":"hybrid","methods":["relevance","milp"]}. Corpus names are restricted identifiers, not filesystem paths. Hybrid retrieval uses BM25 and exact dense chunk search with rank fusion.

Resource and failure policy

There is one inference worker and capacity for four outstanding jobs. A full queue returns 429 and a retry hint. Unknown JSON fields, duplicate source IDs, invalid k and size-limit violations return 422. Input limits are declared in schemas.py: at most 100 comparison sources, 12,000 characters per source, 100,000 combined comparison characters, and up to 500 sources/one million characters for ingestion. The generation limit is 32 new tokens.

If a request includes QAOA and more than ten sources, all its compared selectors use the same label-independent relevance-reduced top-ten pool. This policy is exposed in results. It avoids comparing different candidate opportunities. Requests without QAOA can use the larger validated pool.

A permitted classical fallback is explicitly labeled with its reason and actual method. It is a service reliability behavior, not a successful QAOA research execution. Deadlines are checked between bounded stages; they do not forcibly preempt an ongoing tensor operation. Restarted abandoned jobs become interrupted. Terminal job retention is bounded at 200 entries. The SQLite store is protected against accidentally starting multiple inference workers against it.

Sources are untrusted text. The source-only prompt is a request to the model, not a proof of injection resistance or groundedness. The service has no authentication, public deployment hardening or arbitrary remote-source fetching. Keep the documented loopback binding for the local demonstration.

Verification and observability

The integration script is benchmark_service.py. It checks actual HTTP ingestion, repeated comparisons including simulated QAOA, cache reuse and corpus retrieval using fictional sources. Its five repeated requests provide a scoped p50/p95, not a production latency estimate. The separate untrusted-source diagnostic is one fixture, not a security benchmark.

QRAG_TRACE_CONSOLE=1 emits OpenTelemetry preparation/retrieval/embedding/graph/selection/generation spans into local logs. Structured completion records omit source text. Full job responses and the local SQLite database still contain answers and supplied sources, so use non-sensitive demonstration material. A functional HTTP check and a visual browser review are different checks; no visual review is claimed when no browser surface is available.

phases.title: I · Release and remaining boundaries
phases.why: A result needs enough preserved material for another person to inspect and reconstruct it. A repository release must not be confused with publication acceptance.
phases.how: Packaged source, wheel, manuscript PDF, checksums, compact predictions and frozen coefficient instances. Documented data/model restoration, upstream rights and outstanding author decisions.
phases.math: Checksums bind artifacts to bytes; reconstruction tolerances account for tiny numerical reduction differences, not changed predictions or IDs. A source snapshot and an environment lock preserve different inputs to a calculation.
phases.result: Saved statistical tables and recorded solver cases reconstruct. The original v0.1.0-research preview remains preserved. Current documentation and service revisions are distinguishable from the frozen scientific core.
phases.boundary: Independent scientific review, rights/licensing choices, actual authorship, venue formatting and submission remain external work. No acceptance, novelty certificate or hardware execution is inferred.

deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Artifact checks and independent reconstruction

A result is traceable when a table cell can be followed to question scores, predictions, selected IDs, objective coefficients and the exact code/configuration that produced them. Checksums detect changed bytes; they do not establish scientific correctness. The final auditor additionally recomputes answer scores, source membership, count/token constraints and pair-sum energies, and retokenizes saved prompts against pinned tokenizers. A failed invariant stops assembly rather than silently correcting a scientific record.

Compact public predictions omit large prompts and parameter traces but preserve the fields needed to regenerate tables, with a SHA-256 digest of their compressed file. Public-table reconstruction needs neither model weights nor raw dataset text. This tests statistical reconstruction from released outcomes; it is different from rerunning retrieval, selection and generation. Full local artifacts and split/corpus restoration scripts support that more expensive route.

For numbers that are mathematically equivalent but differ slightly in floating-point reduction order on another machine, reconstruction accepts an absolute/relative tolerance of 10^-12. It still requires identical structure, IDs, counts and file hashes. Tolerance is not permission to substitute different predictions.

A container image and a dependency lock solve different problems

A lock records exact package versions. An image packages an installed operating-system/runtime filesystem. Pinning the base-image digest fixes its bytes, while pinning runtime dependencies prevents a rebuild from silently adopting newer libraries. Neither fixes the host kernel, CPU/GPU hardware or every external driver. The CPU service and CUDA experiments deliberately have different environment snapshots; passing a CPU service check is not evidence of bit-identical GPU outputs.

The container runs as a nonroot user, mounts weights read-only and stores mutable indexes/jobs in a separate named volume. This separates immutable inputs from runtime state. Removing a disposable container need not remove that named volume. Restart recovery can then distinguish completed jobs from interrupted ones. These mechanisms are useful in other model services even when no quantum component exists.

Correctness tests also have dependency boundaries. The lightweight workflow checks the available baseline contracts and explicitly skips integrations whose optional packages are absent. The fuller research workflow installs Qiskit/FAISS/service dependencies and executes those integrations. A skip is visible absence of a check, not a passed execution; the full suite currently has 46 tests. Testing source spectra, feasibility and probability sensitivity with actual Qiskit is different from exercising HTTP state transitions with an explicitly labeled fake inference engine.

deep.label: Derivation and implementation detail
deep.html:
Versioned release versus scientific acceptance

A source archive records one committed tree; a wheel installs its Python packages; a PDF is a readable rendered account; checksums identify the supplied bytes. These objects serve different consumers. The release builder checks their consistency and rejects accidental inclusion of datasets, weights or private notes. Public availability still does not supply an unspecified license, establish novelty or replace peer review. The project therefore separates a reproducible software/research artifact from the human decisions and external publication process.

deep.label: Measured results and boundaries
deep.html:
Phase I — reproducible artifact and external boundaries

The versioned research artifact contains the committed source, configurations, compact outcomes, source snapshots, figures, reports, an installable wheel and the reviewed manuscript PDF, with checksums identifying the files. The release builder requires a clean commit and verifies public prediction hashes, the common core identity and the reviewed PDF/source hashes. It excludes raw/processed datasets, model weights, large local runs, caches and private notes. The CPU container and wheel builds provide separate packaging evidence; no independently awarded artifact badge is claimed.

The claim/evidence map connects findings to exact outputs. Remaining external work identifies independent scientific review, unjudged graph annotations, browser visual review, author/rights-holder decisions, venue-specific formatting and actual submission. Those steps are not silently marked complete. Physical-device execution remains unavailable; simulation is the stated scope. The current local study and manuscript are complete as an implementation/evaluation artifact, not an accepted publication.

deep.label: Final handoff
deep.html:
Remaining external work after the local execution

The laptop implementation, declared experiments, artifact checks, manuscript draft and local service are complete within their documented scope. No research computation is left pending. This file lists decisions or validations that cannot be represented as completed by autonomous implementation.

Item Current state Required next action
Scientific review and publication decision Comparative/negative findings; no demonstrated guidance gain or quantum advantage Independently examine the methods, sources, predictions and contribution. Decide whether the current diagnostic study is substantial enough for the chosen venue or needs further research.
Authorship and institutional details Not invented in the manuscript Confirm actual authors/order, affiliations, corresponding author, contributions, funding and competing interests. All authors approve the final content.
Code, artifact and manuscript licensing No project-wide grant assigned Rights holders choose appropriate licenses and check upstream terms before a formal archival release/submission. The 3B generator uses different terms from the 1.5B model.
Independent graph validation Forty source-grounded edges prepared, all unjudged Use the worksheet and restored full documents to annotate entity identity and useful question bridges. Do not describe the current graph as semantically verified.
Browser visual review HTTP/static/API checks and real inference passed; no enabled browser surface was available Open the local dashboard, review its layout and exercise the controls interactively. This is separate from the completed manuscript PDF visual inspection.
Venue formatting and actual submission Generic editable Markdown and a reviewed PDF exist; no submission performed Choose a venue, apply its current Word/LaTeX/template and citation requirements, complete declarations/disclosures and submit through the official portal. Retain the substantive AI-assistance disclosure.
Independent closest-method reproduction Related methods and estimator differences documented If needed for the final claim, obtain/run the original reference implementations and model settings. Current local coverage is an explicitly different comparator, not an exact SetR/QUBO-paper reproduction.

The current local demonstration runs in the qrag-release-demo CPU container at http://127.0.0.1:8766. It uses the persistent qrag-verification-state volume and a read-only local model-cache mount. The service guide describes restarting it or running a new instance. Old verification containers are stopped. No unrelated user containers or services were changed.

Physical quantum execution was unavailable and remains optional future work; no hardware result is implied. Typed factual relation extraction, quantum token-budget encoding, large-scale production deployment and continuously batched generation were not added. The implementation decisions and limitations explain the bounded study and local engineering scope. They are extensions, not hidden completed features.

No cloud allocation, paid inference, quantum allocation, email, manuscript submission or payment was used. GitHub contains the phase commits and versioned research artifact. The three main documents retain detailed mathematics, measured outcomes and implementation history. A research artifact release or preprint is not peer-reviewed acceptance.

documents.title: Project overview
documents.html:
Q-RAG: research on context selection for RAG

Q-RAG studies how classical optimization and simulated quantum algorithms select context for multi-hop question answering. It combines token-safe retrieval, an entity-link scoring proxy, constrained subset selection, sparse QAOA circuits and real local language-model answer evaluation.

The completed local study is an encoding-aware empirical comparison: 53,230 audited records across 24 conditions, covering 1,000 distinct held-out questions, two generators and separately scoped controls. All quantum execution is classical simulation. The proposed evidence-guidance benefit is not established, and no practical quantum advantage is claimed. Read the manuscript PDF, claim/evidence map and remaining external work.

The research progress report records the mathematical formulation, implementation status, audited results and research decisions. Update it at each phase boundary using the report maintenance checklist.

The technical companion explains concepts, derivations and worked examples. The development sequence connects those concepts to the implementation order and decisions. See the documentation index for the full set.

Start here

The website now includes a complete project journey at /journey: ten connected chapters, the historical baseline and phases A–I, interactive mathematical examples, saved-result comparisons, the full manuscript and an in-site reference library. Follow the guided flow or expand the full derivations. The existing live comparison laboratory remains at /. Reading the journey does not load models or start inference. See the journey build guide.

From the repository root, using the existing laptop environment:

venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
venv/bin/python scripts/download_models.py --core-only
venv/bin/uvicorn qrag_service.app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --workers 1

Open the project journey at http://127.0.0.1:8000/journey or the live laboratory at http://127.0.0.1:8000. Only a submitted inference job needs the pinned local MiniLM and Qwen 1.5B weights. Cold readiness returns 503 until loading succeeds; the reading website remains usable. API inputs contain no reference answers. The service guide explains the API, container, queue, limits and explicit fallback policy.

For a fresh installation, input restoration and model-free result reconstruction, follow reproducibility. Weights and datasets are not bundled. CPU container, CI and CUDA laptop dependencies have distinct recorded snapshots. The historical baseline guide documents the original three-question experiment rather than the complete current study.

What is implemented

  • Sentence-aware token-safe chunks, source offsets, content-addressed embedding/graph caches and checked FAISS/SQLite indexes.
  • Dense, BM25, hybrid, cross-encoder, MMR, coverage, greedy, MILP, annealing and uniform feasible-sampling references.
  • Common relevance/redundancy/entity-link coefficients, native count/token constraints and certified solver-status accounting.
  • Signed sparsification with absolute, random, degree and evidence-guided edge rules; original and surrogate energies retained.
  • Actual Qiskit statevector/shot/noise diagnostics, penalty/XY encodings and complete synthetic-target compilation.
  • Explicit diagnosis of the basis-start depth-one global-phase limitation, plus a separately labeled feasible-preparation control.
  • HotpotQA/MuSiQue answer EM/F1, supporting-document metrics, question-level paired intervals and failure-inclusive answer denominators.
  • Pinned MiniLM/Qwen revisions, actual prompts/token IDs, frozen split/corpus manifests, journal recovery and source snapshots.
  • FastAPI jobs, persistence, local dashboard, OpenTelemetry stage traces, a nonroot CPU container and remote correctness/build CI.

Each main study output contains a manifest, append-only predictions journal, summary and scientific source snapshot. The primary matrix fixes 18 conditions and 50,290 method/question evaluations over 1,000 distinct held-out questions. Solver seeds, methods and generator repeats are not additional independent questions. Secondary controls have separate scopes and manifests.

Research interpretation

Equal passage counts do not imply equal tokens; equal caps do not imply equal consumption. Better objective energy does not imply better answers. A squared count penalty can make a sparse cost graph dense again. Count-preserving mixing has preparation and mixer costs, and a basis-start first diagonal cost layer is only a global phase. Complete compiler measurements are not minimum-cost proofs or hardware speedups.

The original prototype and its document-selection notebooks were retired from the current checkout after verifying that the current package/tests do not depend on them. Their code remains in the preserved research release. Their recall/F1 figures concern document selection and unequal context sizes; they cannot establish answer-quality or quantum improvements. The historical first baseline is documented in the progress report, while the current runner provides the controlled study implementation.

The manuscript source separates principal and exploratory comparisons. The publication guide records current venue options and the remaining author/submission decisions. Rights and attribution identify upstream terms; a project-wide license has not been invented on the owners' behalf. No scholarly submission or acceptance is claimed.

For an inexpensive artifact check after installing the CPU CI dependencies, run:

venv/bin/python scripts/reproduce_public_tables.py --verify
venv/bin/python scripts/reproduce_quantum_instance.py --verify-recorded

These commands reconstruct saved statistics and rerun one frozen solver instance without model weights or dataset downloads. The released coefficient bundle contains 110 optimization instances. Full end-to-end inference is a separate, more expensive reproduction route described in the guide.

sections.title: Q-RAG: research on context selection for RAG
sections.text:
Q-RAG: research on context selection for RAG

Q-RAG studies how classical optimization and simulated quantum algorithms select context for multi-hop question answering. It combines token-safe retrieval, an entity-link scoring proxy, constrained subset selection, sparse QAOA circuits and real local language-model answer evaluation.

The completed local study is an encoding-aware empirical comparison: 53,230 audited records across 24 conditions, covering 1,000 distinct held-out questions, two generators and separately scoped controls. All quantum execution is classical simulation. The proposed evidence-guidance benefit is not established, and no practical quantum advantage is claimed. Read the [manuscript PDF](output/pdf/manuscript.pdf), [claim/evidence map](docs/CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MAP.md) and [remaining external work](docs/HUMAN_HANDOFF.md).

The [research progress report](docs/RESEARCH_PROGRESS_REPORT.md) records the mathematical formulation, implementation status, audited results and research decisions. Update it at each phase boundary using the [report maintenance checklist](docs/research_report/MAINTENANCE.md).

The [technical companion](docs/TECHNICAL_FOUNDATIONS.md) explains concepts, derivations and worked examples. The [development sequence](docs/DEVELOPMENT_SEQUENCE.md) connects those concepts to the implementation order and decisions. See the [documentation index](docs/README.md) for the full set.
