Remaining external work after the local execution

The laptop implementation, declared experiments, artifact checks, manuscript draft and local service are complete within their documented scope. No research computation is left pending. This file lists decisions or validations that cannot be represented as completed by autonomous implementation.

Item Current state Required next action
Scientific review and publication decision Comparative/negative findings; no demonstrated guidance gain or quantum advantage Independently examine the methods, sources, predictions and contribution. Decide whether the current diagnostic study is substantial enough for the chosen venue or needs further research.
Authorship and institutional details Not invented in the manuscript Confirm actual authors/order, affiliations, corresponding author, contributions, funding and competing interests. All authors approve the final content.
Code, artifact and manuscript licensing No project-wide grant assigned Rights holders choose appropriate licenses and check upstream terms before a formal archival release/submission. The 3B generator uses different terms from the 1.5B model.
Independent graph validation Forty source-grounded edges prepared, all unjudged Use the worksheet and restored full documents to annotate entity identity and useful question bridges. Do not describe the current graph as semantically verified.
Browser visual review HTTP/static/API checks and real inference passed; no enabled browser surface was available Open the local dashboard, review its layout and exercise the controls interactively. This is separate from the completed manuscript PDF visual inspection.
Venue formatting and actual submission Generic editable Markdown and a reviewed PDF exist; no submission performed Choose a venue, apply its current Word/LaTeX/template and citation requirements, complete declarations/disclosures and submit through the official portal. Retain the substantive AI-assistance disclosure.
Independent closest-method reproduction Related methods and estimator differences documented If needed for the final claim, obtain/run the original reference implementations and model settings. Current local coverage is an explicitly different comparator, not an exact SetR/QUBO-paper reproduction.

The current local demonstration runs in the qrag-release-demo CPU container at http://127.0.0.1:8766. It uses the persistent qrag-verification-state volume and a read-only local model-cache mount. The service guide describes restarting it or running a new instance. Old verification containers are stopped. No unrelated user containers or services were changed.

Physical quantum execution was unavailable and remains optional future work; no hardware result is implied. Typed factual relation extraction, quantum token-budget encoding, large-scale production deployment and continuously batched generation were not added. The implementation decisions and limitations explain the bounded study and local engineering scope. They are extensions, not hidden completed features.

No cloud allocation, paid inference, quantum allocation, email, manuscript submission or payment was used. GitHub contains the phase commits and versioned research artifact. The three main documents retain detailed mathematics, measured outcomes and implementation history. A research artifact release or preprint is not peer-reviewed acceptance.

documents.title: Publication preparation · dated snapshot
documents.html:
Publication route and remaining author decisions

Checked November 10, 2026. This is a submission-preparation guide, not a record of submission or acceptance. The manuscript's contribution should follow the measured findings: an encoding-aware empirical study with explicit state-preparation and sampling controls. No practical quantum advantage, guaranteed evidence preservation or exhaustive novelty finding is established.

Venue choice

Route Current primary-source information Fit and decision
Quantum Machine Intelligence scope Includes quantum optimization, quantum NLP and quantum/AI software/application studies Recommended initial journal candidate if external review finds the empirical contribution substantial. Regular submission avoids forcing an incomplete result into a conference date.
QCNC 2027 call Paper deadline November 20, 2026; notification January 20, 2027; quantum computing/AI are topics An available deadline before December 2026. Ten days from this check leaves limited independent review time; use only if the contribution and full review are ready.
ACL 2027 call ARR deadline January 4, 2027, 23:59 UTC-12; subsequent conference commitment; no dual submissions Stretch option requiring a convincing NLP contribution. ARR review and conference acceptance are separate steps.
SIGIR 2027 full-paper call Abstract January 14 and paper January 21, 2027, AoE; notification April 5 Stretch option if retrieval evaluation is a substantial contribution. A prior abstract is required. Other tracks have separate calls.

These are scope judgments, not predictions of acceptance. A careful negative-result study can be useful, but evidence that a weak implementation underperforms is not by itself a strong new scientific result. The preparation control and same-draw random reference help distinguish an algorithmic limitation from an implementation artifact. Broader semantic-graph validation and independent review remain valuable before selecting the final venue.

Journal preparation

The Quantum Machine Intelligence instructions require editable manuscript sources, author details and declarations. Mathematical manuscripts may use LaTeX. Its abstract range is 150–250 words and it requests 4–6 keywords. All authors must approve submission, and the work cannot simultaneously be under consideration elsewhere. AI use beyond copy editing must be documented; accountability remains with human authors. The current manuscript contains an assistance disclosure and must receive substantive human review.

The publisher's options include subscription publication without an article-processing charge and optional paid open access. The displayed open-access price depends on acceptance date and taxes; no paid route is selected here. Conference registration/presentation costs are separate. Recheck the official pages before committing funds or submitting.

The current paper is a review draft. Its general presentation is not claimed to satisfy every venue-specific citation/template requirement. Final author names, affiliations, contributions, competing interests, funding and repository licensing must reflect actual facts. Do not fill them with invented declarations. Maintain a dated final literature search, especially for close QUBO/RAG work, before claiming novelty.

Submission steps

  1. Review methods, saved question-level predictions, statistical assumptions, limitations and the claim-to-evidence map. Resolve substantive errors before formatting.
  2. Agree the author list/order, corresponding author, affiliations, contributions and any institutional requirements. Each author reviews and accepts responsibility for the final content.
  3. Choose one venue and article type. Apply its current editable template, citation style, anonymity policy, word/page limits and disclosure rules. Verify all references against primary sources.
  4. Choose code/artifact and manuscript licenses with the rights holders. Check third-party dataset/model terms. Create an archival artifact version if appropriate; a GitHub tag alone is not a preservation guarantee or an awarded reproducibility badge.
  5. Upload through the venue's official submission link. Supply the manuscript, editable source, figures, supplement, availability statement and required declarations. Check the generated submission PDF before final confirmation.
  6. Retain the submission receipt. If reviews arrive, answer them point by point and distinguish new experiments from the frozen original evaluation. Acceptance, proofs, registration and presentation may add later work.

No portal submission, email, reviewer nomination, authorship agreement or payment is performed by this implementation run.

Preprint and timeline

An arXiv posting is a preprint, not peer-reviewed acceptance. Official submission guidance requires a registered submitting author, appropriate scientific content and a distribution license. Endorsement guidance explains that new categories/authors may require endorsement. Follow the chosen venue's preprint/anonymity policy and obtain coauthor agreement before posting.

There is no fixed project deadline. Use completion criteria: finished audited experiments, defensible interpretation, independently reviewed manuscript and verified submission files. Allow real time for review and corrections. Journal peer review has no guaranteed acceptance date; conference dates are submission opportunities, not reasons to lower the evidence standard. The historical schedule in the implementation plan is superseded by this completion-first policy.

documents.title: Historical baseline execution
documents.html:
Historical first baseline runner

This guide describes the preserved first research slice: fixed-count relevance ranking versus MILP on the same candidate pools, followed by local answer generation. Its limits refer to that runner. The current study also implements graph features, QAOA, token budgets, chunking, caches and corpus search; use the reproducibility guide for that pipeline. The original prototype was retired from the current checkout and remains in the research release snapshot.

Environment and installation

Run commands from the repository root. The tested local environment uses Python 3.14.4, NumPy 2.5.3, SciPy 1.18.1, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, Transformers 5.17.0 and SentenceTransformers 6.1.0. CUDA was unavailable through this execution environment; the smoke experiment ran on CPU with four PyTorch threads and float32 weights. A CUDA-enabled PyTorch build does not imply that a usable GPU is visible.

For the existing environment:

venv/bin/python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

For a fresh environment with Python 3.14:

python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-baselines.lock
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e '.[models]'
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

The core lock pins the tested NumPy/SciPy pair. The fresh model installation resolves its own runtime dependencies; compare them with the recorded environment before trying to reproduce a particular result. Manifests capture tested runtime versions. The later laptop, CI and CPU-container locks are described in the reproducibility guide; the laptop snapshot is host-specific. The original broad requirements list is retained with the archived prototype, rather than serving as the current installation contract.

The real experiment requires the existing processed development JSON and the exact model snapshots configured in configs/dev_baselines.toml. The CLI defaults to local-only model resolution. If a snapshot is unavailable, obtain the specified model revision before running; the offline command will fail rather than quietly download or substitute another revision. Unit tests need neither models nor the real dataset.

Run and inspect

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false venv/bin/python -m qrag.experiments.run \
  --config configs/dev_baselines.toml --output results/my_baseline_run

Use a new output directory for a new run. To resume an interrupted run or recreate the summary from an already completed run:

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false venv/bin/python -m qrag.experiments.run \
  --config configs/dev_baselines.toml --output results/my_baseline_run --resume

Resume rejects changes in computation configuration, dataset bytes, question IDs, package source, recorded environment or backend identity. Completed records, including recorded per-method failures, are not retried or duplicated. After correcting a failure, use a new run directory. Saved records are atomically replaced after each method so interruption cannot leave a half-written JSON line. Do not run concurrent writers against one directory.

Artifacts

Artifact Contents
manifest.json Actual configuration, dataset/source hashes, question IDs, pinned model snapshots, runtime packages/device, Git state, model preparation and invocation timing
predictions.jsonl One record per question/method, selected source IDs, energies/coefficient arrays, solver status/bounds, exact prompt, generated answer, tokens, metrics or error
summary.json Per-method answer averages including failures, failure counts, successful-only evidence/token/generation summaries
failure.json Traceback for startup or interrupted-run failure, when applicable

Results are ignored by Git because they may be large. Keep important result directories or archive them separately. A source hash identifies the code but is not a source archive: retain the corresponding checkout/diff when sharing runs. The published smoke notes are small tracked documentation.

Experimental controls and interpretation

Both selectors receive the same MiniLM scores and the same full candidate text. The objective minimizes negative relevance plus positive-similarity redundancy, with alpha=1 and beta=0.2 in the example configuration. These settings are inherited starting values, not newly tuned or established optimal values.

MILP solves the exact-count problem through binary x variables and continuous y variables constrained to equal each pair product. Exhaustive enumeration checks small signed-coefficient instances in tests. MILP status and bounds determine whether a solution is certified optimal; a time-limited feasible solution may still be used and is labeled accordingly.

The ranking baseline maximizes individual relevance rather than the full relevance–redundancy objective. Its selections are additionally evaluated using that same full objective for comparison. Neither solver receives gold labels. Gold supporting titles and reference answers enter only the evaluator.

The example requests exactly five documents. If fewer candidates exist, short_pool_policy="use_all" explicitly applies exactly min(5, candidate count) to both methods; "error" instead records the case as an error. Context follows original candidate order for both methods. The generator, prompt policy, tokenizer and decoding settings are common.

The sample does not enforce equal tokens, so report actual lengths and avoid attributing a quality difference solely to selection. Generation uses chat formatting and reserves output space. Context exceeding the configured total token limit fails visibly; it is not silently trimmed.

Embedding inputs exceeding MiniLM's actual maximum fail by default. An explicit embedding_truncation="report" mode is available for legacy-style diagnostics and records affected inputs (position zero is the question). It is not a substitute for the planned chunking implementation. Until chunking exists, larger datasets may produce recorded overlength failures.

Models load once per invocation; features are computed once per question and shared across its selectors. There is no persistent embedding cache. Preparation time, shared feature time, solver time and per-method generation time are recorded separately. Do not sum duplicated shared-feature fields to estimate actual wall time; use the invocation wall time in the manifest. Generation is actually repeated for each method, even if selections coincide.

Metric definitions and data quality

Answer EM/F1 follow HotpotQA's reference rules, including punctuation/article normalization, repeated-token counts and special yes/no/noanswer handling. Empty-normalized answer pairs have EM=1 and F1=0 under those rules. Semantic synonyms can still receive zero token overlap; preserve this metric and supplement it with documented error analysis rather than silently altering it.

Document recall and complete-support coverage use annotated document titles. They are not sentence-level supporting-fact F1 or proof that the model used those sources. Missing supporting annotations produce null document metrics. All-question answer averages assign zero to failed method/question records; evidence and token summaries are successful-only and labeled as such. A nonzero CLI exit status flags recorded errors.

The first three development examples are already inspected and must not become a supposedly untouched evaluation set. Keep reference anomalies unchanged in the primary run and document them; any corrected-label analysis must be separate and justified independently of which method wins.

Teaching exercise

The MILP linearization uses 0 <= y <= 1, y <= x_i, y <= x_j, and y >= x_i + x_j - 1 for binary x. Work out y for (x_i,x_j)=(0,1) and (1,1). Explain why y need not be declared integer. The learning log records the answer only after the learner supplies it.

Neither solver receives gold labels. Gold supporting titles and reference answers enter only the evaluator.

The example requests exactly five documents. If fewer candidates exist, short_pool_policy="use_all" explicitly applies exactly min(5, candidate count) to both methods; "error" instead records the case as an error. Context follows original candidate order for both methods. The generator, prompt policy, tokenizer and decoding settings are common.

The sample does not enforce equal tokens, so report actual lengths and avoid attributing a quality difference solely to selection. Generation uses chat formatting and reserves output space. Context exceeding the configured total token limit fails visibly; it is not silently trimmed.

Embedding inputs exceeding MiniLM's actual maximum fail by default. An explicit embedding_truncation="report" mode is available for legacy-style diagnostics and records affected inputs (position zero is the question). It is not a substitute for the planned chunking implementation. Until chunking exists, larger datasets may produce recorded overlength failures.

Models load once per invocation; features are computed once per question and shared across its selectors. There is no persistent embedding cache. Preparation time, shared feature time, solver time and per-method generation time are recorded separately. Do not sum duplicated shared-feature fields to estimate actual wall time; use the invocation wall time in the manifest. Generation is actually repeated for each method, even if selections coincide.

Metric definitions and data quality

Answer EM/F1 follow [HotpotQA's reference rules](https://github.com/hotpotqa/hotpot/blob/master/hotpot_evaluate_v1.py), including punctuation/article normalization, repeated-token counts and special yes/no/noanswer handling. Empty-normalized answer pairs have EM=1 and F1=0 under those rules. Semantic synonyms can still receive zero token overlap; preserve this metric and supplement it with documented error analysis rather than silently altering it.

Document recall and complete-support coverage use annotated document titles. They are not sentence-level supporting-fact F1 or proof that the model used those sources. Missing supporting annotations produce null document metrics. All-question answer averages assign zero to failed method/question records; evidence and token summaries are successful-only and labeled as such. A nonzero CLI exit status flags recorded errors.

The first three development examples are already inspected and must not become a supposedly untouched evaluation set. Keep reference anomalies unchanged in the primary run and document them; any corrected-label analysis must be separate and justified independently of which method wins.

Teaching exercise

The MILP linearization uses 0 <= y <= 1, y <= x_i, y <= x_j, and y >= x_i + x_j - 1 for binary x. Work out y for (x_i,x_j)=(0,1) and (1,1). Explain why y need not be declared integer. The learning log records the answer only after the learner supplies it.

Development-derived sampling mechanism study

To separate trained distribution quality from best-of-many selection, we train p=1 circuits on 20 development-derived coefficient instances at each of n=8,10,12,16, with k=5 and three seeds per encoding. These are 480 numerical circuit solves, not additional held-out answer evaluations. For single-draw optimum mass u, the probability of seeing an optimum in S draws is 1-(1-u)^S. We compute this directly from the trained ideal statevector distribution and enumerate feasible energies. This calculation does not estimate a physical device's output distribution.

glossary.RAG: Retrieval augmented generation: supply retrieved source text to a generator so it can answer using external information.
glossary.Evidence: Information that supports answering a particular question. Relevance alone does not establish support.
glossary.Inference inputs: Fields available to the deployed calculation: question, source text, identities and provenance. They exclude answer keys.
glossary.Reference annotations / gold labels: Expected answers and annotated supporting passages used for evaluation, not ordinary selection.
glossary.Corpus: A collection of source documents searched before a candidate subset is selected.
glossary.Token: A model-specific text unit. Token counts are not word counts and differ across tokenizers.
glossary.Chunking: Split long documents into bounded, traceable units that fit the embedding encoder.
glossary.Embedding: A learned numerical representation of text. It is not a list of verified facts.
glossary.Cosine similarity: Normalized vector dot product. Unit-vector dot product equals cosine, not a calibrated support probability.
glossary.Lazy loading: Load model weights when first needed rather than when the service process starts.
glossary.Embedding cache: Persist already computed vectors under keys identifying content and the representation recipe.
glossary.Persistent index: A saved searchable vector structure with consistent metadata so it can be restored across process restarts.
glossary.FAISS: A vector-search library. This project uses exact inner-product chunk search with normalized vectors.
glossary.BM25: Lexical retrieval using term rarity, term-frequency saturation and document-length normalization.
glossary.Reranker: A more expensive question/passage joint model used to reorder candidate results.
glossary.MMR: Maximal marginal relevance: choose relevant items while discouraging redundancy with already selected items.
glossary.QUBO: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization. Our native count/token problem is constrained; a penalty can encode count into a QUBO.
glossary.ILP / MILP: Integer / mixed-integer linear programming. Binary pair products are linearized with auxiliary variables and exact inequalities.
glossary.Objective: A mathematical preference over selections. Minimizing it need not maximize generated-answer correctness.
glossary.Dense formulation: Many variable pairs have nonzero interactions. This can increase storage, optimization and compiled circuit work.
glossary.Evidence modelling: Turn question/source signals into estimated usefulness and complementarity features. The current entity-link proxy is not verified factual reasoning.
glossary.Ising Hamiltonian: A quantum operator with fields and pair couplings whose basis-state energies encode a binary objective.
glossary.QAOA: A parameterized quantum cost/mixer circuit with a classical angle optimizer. Here its quantum evolution is classically simulated.
glossary.COBYLA: Constrained Optimization BY Linear Approximation: a derivative-free optimizer used to adjust circuit angles.
glossary.Statevector: The complex amplitudes describing a pure quantum state. Explicit simulation requires exponentially growing storage.
glossary.Shot: One circuit measurement sample. Finite-shot sampling differs from reading an exact statevector distribution.
glossary.StatevectorSampler: A Qiskit primitive that samples simulated quantum states. Used by the retired wrapper, not proof of QPU execution.
glossary.NumPyMinimumEigensolver: A classical lowest-eigenvalue solver used by the retired exact wrapper; it is not a physical quantum processor.
glossary.MinimumEigenOptimizer: A Qiskit adapter that maps supported optimization problems to operators and interprets solver output. The underlying solver can be classical.
glossary.XY mixer: An exchange-based circuit that preserves the number of selected bits ideally. Noise can break this property.
glossary.Global phase: A common unit-magnitude complex factor on the whole state; it cancels from measurement probabilities.
glossary.Sparsification: Remove some pair interactions while retaining a declared budget and tracking the objective change.
glossary.Ablation: Remove or change a component under controlled conditions to investigate what it contributes.
glossary.Precision / recall: Overlap divided by predicted items / reference items. Always specify whether the items are answer tokens or evidence documents.
glossary.Recall@k: Annotated relevant items recovered among the first k retrieved/selected items, under a declared identity and denominator.
glossary.F1: Harmonic mean of precision and recall. Answer-token F1 and document-selection F1 evaluate different targets.
glossary.Paired bootstrap: Resample the same question IDs together across methods to quantify uncertainty in their mean difference.
glossary.Pilot: A small preliminary run used to check feasibility, settings and variability before freezing the final experiment.
glossary.Profiling: Measure where time, memory or other resources are used for a stated workload.
glossary.Cold / cached run: A cold run includes first-use loading/computation; a cached run can reuse existing state. Warm models and warm caches are different conditions.
glossary.Pinned dependencies: Software versions fixed for repeatable installation. They do not themselves prove scientific correctness.
glossary.Manifest: Recorded settings plus actual identities and execution metadata for a run.
glossary.FastAPI: A Python web API framework used here to validate requests and expose local inference jobs.
glossary.GPU batching: Process several embedding inputs together to amortize overhead, while respecting memory limits.
glossary.Quantum advantage: A demonstrated advantage under a clearly defined comparison with strong classical alternatives. Quantum involvement alone is insufficient.
glossary.Noninferiority: Evidence that a method is not worse by more than a predeclared acceptable margin. A nonsignificant difference does not establish this.
